- **`prismeri-first-wings-painting.jpg`** — Halle Ostrander's finished painting
  on panel, worked up afterwards from Plate I: the First Wings form hanging at
  work with shaped glass. A new file beside the plate, which it supersedes on
  the Prismeri page and never overwrites. Landscape 16:9, 1600px wide.
  References: `story-bible/reference-art/prismeri-body-bat-2026-10-14.jpg`, `src/images/lore/prismeri-lattice-gathering-painting.jpg`
  > Two images are attached. The first, a photograph of a bat, is a reference for body plan only: take the body plan, the proportions and the resting pose from it (a flier hanging head-down by its hind feet, the wings as forelimbs with the long finger bones running through the membrane, the short neck, the head carried close against the shoulders, no tail), and nothing else: not the species, not the face, not the fur or its colour, not the branch, not the setting, not the open wing, and not the bat's hand, which is a different shape and is described below. The second, a painting, is a reference for medium, light and handling only: match its hyperreal oil-on-panel finish, its warm amber haze, its soft background of pale crystal spires and its palette, and take nothing else from it: not its figures, not their faces, not their pose, not the ledge or the shell. A finished natural-history painting in oil on a gessoed wooden panel, hyperrealist, worked up by a field naturalist from field sheets drawn from life, painted to be as close to a photograph as a painter's hand can get, in the manner of the finest museum wildlife painting: true scale and true anatomy, natural light falling from one direction, real atmosphere with warm haze thickening into the distance, every surface painted exactly (soft chitin, thin veined membrane, frosted glass, cut glass), a shallow depth of field with the background soft and the subject crisp. No outlines, no ink lines, no washes, no visible sketch. The medium shows only faintly, at close inspection, as the finest hand-made study betrays itself. The scene is on Prismere, a low-gravity world under thick hazy air full of suspended crystalline dust, whose living things are built from glass and crystal. The subject is a First Wings Prismeri, an adult of a sapient people, not an animal and not a monster: a light, long, slender body on a level spine, lean and thin-limbed like a dried leaf, with no bulk of muscle anywhere and no fur anywhere, its soft still-hardening exoskeleton a pale grey-violet with a dull matte sheen like unfired porcelain, faintly segmented; the wings are the forelimbs, the gossamer membrane so thin it is nearly transparent, stretched from one elongated outer digit back to the hind leg; long-toed prehensile hind feet; a short neck, the blunt rounded head carried close against the shoulders, a smooth closed dome like a helmet with no features on its back or crown except one mark: a single narrow continuous stripe of smooth pale frosted glass, inlaid flush with the surface, running lengthwise along the very top of the skull from the brow back to the nape, like one seam or one pale line down the middle of the crown, unbroken, without segments, without separate pieces, without edges that catch the light, as plain as a stripe painted down a smooth egg. That stripe is the only thing the skull carries. No ears, no tail, the body ending at the hind legs with the membrane running between wing and leg. It hangs head-down at rest from the shaped ledge of a lumenspire, a tall translucent mineral tower lit faintly from within in amber, its long-toed hind feet gripping the ledge and taking the whole weight, both wings folded close about the body, neither spread. The hands: the membrane is carried on a single long outer digit, and at the wrist of each folded wing, in front of that digit, the hand stands free of the membrane as a simple Y, three thin jointed fingers and nothing more, spread like the three prongs of a trident or the three toes of a bird's foot, one finger pointing up and two pointing down, each ending in one small curved claw. The glass is one small three-cornered prism of clear cut glass, lit from behind by the amber haze, and the two hands hold that one prism together below the head, each hand's Y laid flat against a face of the prism so the thin dark fingers show as a plain Y-shaped silhouette against the glowing glass, one fingertip at each corner of the triangle, turning it slowly in the light. The viewpoint is from above and behind, a three-quarter rear view from slightly higher than the ledge, so we look down over its back and shoulders: the head is turned away from us, bent down toward the glass in its fingers, and only the back and crown of the head with its one pale stripe are seen; the eyes are hidden or at most a dark edge seen from behind, and the mouth is not visible at all, hidden by the turned head. The hands and the glass are the clearest thing in the painting. Seen from a working distance of several metres, the whole figure small in the frame, about a third of the frame's height, with the ledge above it, open air round it and a long drop below it, so that the painting is of a worker at a ledge and not a portrait; warm amber haze behind with soft pale crystal spires, and far below a forest of crystal, bare glassy spikes and columns of pale quartz, nothing green and nothing that grows on Earth. The four corners of the panel hold only haze, spire and crystal, with nothing written, marked or signed anywhere on the panel. Quiet, absorbed, at work. Negative: the face turned toward the viewer, a face seen from below, a visible mouth, a grin, a smile, an open mouth, teeth, crystal teeth, a toothed band, a jaw, fangs, tongue; a ring or band round the head, a crown, a diadem, a tiara, a circlet, a headband, a collar, a necklace, a row of small crystals, beads, gems, studs, jewels, scales on the head, segments on the head, plates on the head; The bat of the same day gives the body plan and the pose only; the painted register allows a painter's finish on the face, which the generator's photographs rendered as animated-film creatures.)*

  *(Revised for rounds 4 to 6, 14 October 2026, on Fable, from the third round's finding. Three changes, and the first two are what worked: the facet band is written as one narrow continuous stripe of smooth frosted glass inlaid flush along the midline of the crown from brow to nape, like a seam down a smooth egg, the only mark the skull carries, with rings, crowns, diadems, collars, rows of small crystals, beads and gems negated, so there is nothing a mouth or a toothed band resembles; the hand is written as a shape and not a count, a Y of three thin fingers like the prongs of a trident or the toes of a bird's foot, laid flat against a face of one back-lit triangular prism so the fingers show as a dark Y on the lit glass, with the number words, the bat's hand and the numeric negatives removed from the text so they cannot prime a four; and the figure is placed small in the frame with the ledge above and the drop below, lean and thin-limbed, both wings shut, the open wing, a second prism, the shell and conifers negated by name, and the four corners declared empty haze. Round 4 ran the first change alone and the teeth were gone from both variations; round 5 added the rest.)*
  *(**Superseded the same evening** by `prismeri-first-wings-painting-2.jpg`, the entry below, at Dermot's choice of one more round after seeing this one; the file was removed from `src/images/lore/` because the validator fails on an unreferenced image, and this entry stays as the record of the prompt and the rounds.)*
  *(**Filed from round 5 variation 1**, 14 October 2026: the view from above and behind, the head bent to the prism with the seam along its crown and no face, both wings folded, hanging by the feet from the spire's ledges, in the register of the filed pair. Flaws passed: the hands read as three or four fingers even at three times magnification, not plainly three, which is less than the filed Full Wings carries; the hind feet grip two separate lips of the spire; the crystal forest below has some bare twig-like forms at the left edge. The other five variations are described under *Finished paintings* in the Prismere set's heading.)*
  *(Third round run 14 October 2026, one round only (Dermot's change of plan the same evening: difficult images may go to Fable, so a failed round stops here): **not filed**, Plate I stays. Variation 1 is seen from behind with the head bent to the glass, and the register matches the filed pair, but the facet band is painted as a ring of crystal teeth round the back of the skull, each hand has four clawed digits, and a signature sits in the lower right corner. Variation 2 hangs with the face visible from the side and below, and the facet band again sits where a mouth would be, as a toothed grin. The finding for the next attempt: the grin of every First Wings round is the facet band itself, which the generator reads as teeth whenever it is described as a row of small crystals near the face; the band should be described as something no mouth resembles (a smooth inlaid strip of glass, or a single pale seam), or left out of a rear view altogether.)*

  > Three images are attached. The first, a painted figure hanging from a ledge, is the reference for the body: paint this same individual, with this body plan, these proportions, this bat-like build, this short neck with the head carried close against the shoulders, this soft grey-violet skin with its dull matte sheen, these thin veined membranes, these long-toed feet; keep its body exactly and change only what is described below, the pose of its wings, the thing in its hands, the mark on its head and the direction of its face. The second, a photograph of a bat, is a reference for pose only: a flier hanging head-down by its hind feet with one wing partly open so the whole membrane is seen from the long outer digit back to the hind leg; take nothing else from it, not its species, face, fur, branch or setting. The third, a painting, is the reference for medium, light and handling: match its hyperreal oil-on-panel finish, its warm amber haze, its soft background of pale crystal spires and its palette, and take nothing else from it, not its figures, their pose, the ledge or the shell. A finished natural-history painting in oil on a gessoed wooden panel, hyperrealist, worked up by a field naturalist from field sheets drawn from life, painted to be as close to a photograph as a painter's hand can get, in the manner of the finest museum wildlife painting: true scale and true anatomy, natural light falling from one direction, real atmosphere with warm haze thickening into the distance, every surface painted exactly (soft chitin, thin veined membrane, frosted glass, cut glass), a shallow depth of field with the background soft and the subject crisp. No outlines, no ink lines, no washes, no visible sketch. The scene is on Prismere, a low-gravity world under thick hazy air full of suspended crystalline dust, whose living things are built from glass and crystal. The subject is a First Wings Prismeri, an adult of a sapient people, not an animal and not a monster, a flier built like a bat and nothing like a person: the wings are the forelimbs, and there are no arms. It hangs head-down at rest by its long-toed hind feet from the shaped ledge of a lumenspire, a tall translucent mineral tower lit faintly from within in amber. Its wings are held part open, not folded and not spread wide, the way a bat holds them when it is busy with something: each wing lifted a little away from the body so the whole gossamer membrane is plainly seen, thin and veined and nearly transparent with the amber light coming through it, stretched from the single long outer digit of the wing back along the body to the hind leg, where it ends; the membrane is the largest thing in the picture after the haze, and anyone looking at the painting sees at once that these are wings. The body ends at the hind legs. Nothing hangs below the body, nothing trails beside the head, and nothing extends past the feet: no tail, no trailing limb, no loose membrane edge hanging free. The head is carried close against the shoulders on a short neck, smooth and closed like a helmet with no ears, and the only mark it carries is a single narrow continuous stripe of smooth pale frosted glass inlaid flush along the top of the skull from the brow back to the nape, like one seam or one pale line down the middle of the crown, unbroken, without segments, without separate pieces, as plain as a stripe painted down a smooth egg. The head is bent down and turned toward the thing in its hands, so the face is mostly turned away toward the work, seen at most as a closed profile with one half-lidded dark eye and a small hard mouth shut to a thin seam, and no teeth. The hands: at the wrist of each wing, in front of the long outer digit, the hand stands free of the membrane as a simple Y, three thin jointed fingers and nothing more, spread like the three prongs of a trident or the three toes of a bird's foot, one finger pointing up and two pointing down, each ending in one small curved claw. The thing in its hands is one small three-cornered prism of clear cut glass, lit from behind by the amber haze, and the two hands hold that one prism together below the head, each hand's Y laid flat against a face of the prism so the thin dark fingers show as a plain Y-shaped silhouette against the glowing glass, one fingertip at each corner of the triangle, turning it slowly in the light. The viewpoint is a three-quarter view from the side and a little above the ledge, chosen so that the near wing's membrane is seen in full and the far wing shows behind it: the hanging body a little off centre, the ledge above it, open air round it and a long drop below, the whole figure about two fifths of the frame's height, so that the painting is of a flier at work at a ledge and not a portrait. Warm amber haze behind with soft pale crystal spires, and far below a forest of crystal, bare glassy spikes and columns of pale quartz, nothing green and nothing that grows on Earth. The four corners of the panel hold only haze, spire and crystal, with nothing written, marked or signed anywhere on the panel. Quiet, absorbed, at work. ### 5b. Outstanding lore illustrations — all 54: 52 prompted 19 August 2026, the pair below 5 October 2026 and delivered the same day

**Visible to the pipeline since 5 October 2026, and not before.**
`scripts/image-prompts.js` matched the heading *Missing lore illustrations*
and this one says *Outstanding*, so every mode of the script skipped the
whole section for seven weeks: `--list` reported nothing pending while this
note said *none generated; all proposals*, and the Step 1 of the runbook
above was answering for 5a alone. Found when the two prompts added on
5 October did not show up either. The match now takes either word, which
means **`--list` reports 54 pending from this section** and a bare
`--generate` would attempt all of them: Step 2's *generate ONE first* is the
guard, and `--only <name>` the tool.

**The pair, prompted 5 October 2026 at Dermot's *Yes please*:**
`what-a-life-is-built-from.md` (7 September 2026, the four requirements and
the heredities found in DNA's place) and its sibling
`what-a-mind-is-carried-by.md` (18 September 2026, the four things any
carrier of a mind has to do and the carriers the record has met). Both are
abstract pages, so both take the section's rule, a concrete anchor each,
and they are carded as a pair: the same station on the same night, the same
cold light and the same film, one on a bench and one at a table, so that
the two pages read as the two halves they are. Their entries are the last
two under *Cosmology* below.

Written in one pass at Dermot's request. **1600×900, 16:9 landscape**, JPG ~85,
into `src/images/lore/`. **None generated; all proposals.**

**The governing rule for this set: every abstract page gets a concrete anchor.**
Roughly half of these are pages about a *rule*, a *scope*, or an *epistemology*
rather than a place, and an abstract page illustrated abstractly produces exactly
the flat filler the house target rules out — *if a prompt reads like a brief for a
passport photograph it fails this*, and a gradient with a glow in it fails it
worse. So each one is anchored on a place, an object, or a person doing
something, and the idea is carried by what that thing is doing. The corpus
already proves the method works: `embodied-cognition.jpg`,
`who-governs-a-universe.jpg`, `things-that-are-made.jpg` and
`teleportation-limitations.jpg` are all abstract pages with concrete frames.

**Standing negative — paste into every one:**
> readable text, lettering, numerals, signage, labels, branding or written characters of any script anywhere in frame; schematic diagrams, technical drawings, blueprints, charts, graphs, arrows, callouts, infographic styling; holograms, projected light, glowing displays, screens, monitors, consoles; visible lamp, light fitting or bulb; lens flare, god rays, magical sparkle, glowing energy, neon; flat gradient background, stock illustration, clip art.

**One naming collision, flagged.** `src/lore/saint-aoife.md` and
`src/characters/saint-aoife.md` are different pages about the same person, and
both would reach for `saint-aoife.jpg`. Different directories, so the build is
fine, but two files one letter apart in intent is how the July audit's alt-text
drift started. The lore page's image is proposed as **`cill-aoife-devotion.jpg`**
and framed on the devotion rather than the woman.

#### Cosmology (12)

Impressions, never schematics. The Cascade tiers in particular must not become
nested-sphere diagrams.

- **`archecluster.jpg`** — *one Archewright's vocabulary carried in every route chart, statute book and certified machine.*
  > A vast orbital archive hall seen from a high gallery, rank upon rank of identical plain shelving running away in perfect repetition into soft distance, every bay built to the same proportion. Two small figures far below at floor level for scale. Cool even daylight from a high clerestory, no fittings visible. The repetition is the subject: one vocabulary, everywhere, unremarked. Pale stone, brushed alloy, deep shadow between the ranks. Immense, ordered, quiet.
  - **Delivered 7 October 2026**, variation 1 of 2 (`gemini-3.1-flash-image`, 2K), through `import-image.ps1` at finish strength 1: symmetry from the gallery; 2 looked down from a stair and lost the repetition.
  - **Not re-rolled, 11 October 2026** (photorealism audit, batch 1). The page's subject is immaterial: a family of universes drawn from one Archewright's vocabulary, which *from inside … looks like nothing at all* (the page's own first paragraph), and the 7 October rule gives an abstract concept a card or nothing, never a picture. The archive hall was the 19 August concrete anchor, and it came back as a CGI visualisation; a photographic re-roll would only be a better picture of a metaphor. **Recommended:** a designed card (`make-codex-cover.ps1` or `make-emblem-card.ps1`, Cosmology) in place of the hall; the alternative is no image, a page without one being complete. Left to Dermot; the prompt above stays as the record of the filed frame.

The prompt above is kept as the record of what the hall was.

- **`archewright.jpg`** — *eternal, unobserved, and known only by inference.*
  > A worked stone quarry face at dawn, seen straight on, where every block that ever left it has been cut to the same handful of standard proportions — the negative shapes still legible in the rock. No tools, no workers, no machinery, nobody present and no sign of anyone recently. Cold clear early light raking across the cut faces. What made the shapes is absent and only the shapes remain. Grey stone, pale sky, long shadow.

**Checking these on return.** Four carry a default strong enough to fail quietly:
**`quantum-computing-and-the-cavern-constraint`** (the gold cryostat),

so does a frame with nothing implied), and **`ollune`** (the trailing-tentacle
jellyfish). Beyond those, the set's own risk is sameness: a great many of these
are *a quiet room with one object in it*, which is the right answer individually
and would be a monotonous gallery. **Judge them as a page of thumbnails, not one
at a time**, and re-roll for variety rather than for quality where they cluster.

#### Two delivered portraits versus the bureau uniform (19 August 2026)

Dermot's direction that **Eden's detectives are uniformed with rank insignia**
(`src/lore/eden-bureau-uniform.md`) postdates two delivered portraits that show
neither. Recorded here rather than acted on, because the runbook's own rule
settles it: **art is illustrative, the prose is canon — when the two disagree,
the entry wins and the art stays.**

**Both are fine, and the second one stopped being a problem the same day.** An
earlier version of this note called Albercombe's herringbone *not compatible*.
Dermot's follow-up — **the obligation is on the lower ranks** — settled it:
Albercombe is a Detective Inspector and Oyelaran a Superintendent, and neither is
required to wear the jacket at all.

- **`rasa-oyelaran.jpg`** — *a plain grey work jacket over a maroon shirt.* Fine
  twice over: she is senior enough not to be required, and a plain grey work
  jacket would pass as the uniform anyway.
- **`wendell-albercombe.jpg`** — *a worn herringbone jacket over an open blue
  shirt.* Fine. A Detective Inspector in civilian cloth is the entry working, not
  the entry contradicted.

**No alt text changes**, and none were needed. Both lines describe what their
files actually show, which is the one hard requirement.

**A future frame of a junior officer takes the uniform** — the jacket, and the
collar mark by rank — where a senior one need not, an undercover one must not,
and a Commissioner is never required to. Note the lettering trap while writing
any of them: the marks are strokes and blocks carrying **no letters and no
numerals**, and whether the jacket bears any identifying number is deliberately
unsettled in the entry, so no prompt should invent one.

**And the same caution now applies to Ranger frames.** Corps and branch badges
are canon as of the same direction, which puts a new device on a uniform that
previously had only tabs and plates — so a Ranger prompt may name a corps badge,
but it is **shapes only**, never a word, a monogram or an emblem with writing in
it.

#### Century audit, entries written new (12 October 2026)

Two images on the century audit's list had no prompt of record (the photorealism audit's cause 4). Each is written fresh from its page here, inside a parsed section so `image-prompts.js --only` can send it.

- **`cerebraun.jpg`** — the Cerebraun species page: a multi-brained people, eight primary limbs each with its own ganglion, chromatophore skin that carries a second channel beneath the spoken one. The filed frame was a CGI brutalist hall with a robed humanoid figure, which gave the people a body the page refuses. The page does not say whether they live in water or air; the S03E01 chapters put Sohrel at a desk on a relay station with humans (*the limb beneath the desk*), so the frame is a Cerebraun at work in air, taken from across the room. Guessed: size (about a person's), the colour of the skin, the room, and (round 2, after round 1 drew an Earth octopus at a desk twice, which asserts the kinship the record refuses) smooth ribbon limbs with no suckers and the tall hooded mantle; the swelling near each limb's tip is the page's ganglion.
  > Documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light, 16:9 landscape, taken from across a quiet office so the subject is small in the frame: a Cerebraun, a sapient person of a many-limbed, multi-brained people, at work as an administrator in the plain office of a relay station in the year 2826, resting on a low broad padded perch beside a plain pale desk. About the size of a person: a soft upright mantle, a central body with two large calm dark eyes, and eight long limbs. THIS IS NOT AN EARTH OCTOPUS OR SQUID, only a people whose remote ancestors filled a similar niche on another world: no suckers anywhere, the limbs smooth, broad and slightly flattened like heavy ribbons, each with a small rounded swelling a little way from its tip where its own ganglion sits, three of them resting along the edge of the desk and one lying still beneath it, the others folded on the perch; the mantle a tall smooth hood rather than a bulbous head. The skin is real living skin, moist-looking and finely textured, a muted mottled grey-brown, and along one arm a slow patch of colour change, a faint warm band moving across a few centimetres of skin, the only sign of the second channel. Calm, attentive, dignified, a colleague at work. The room is clean and kept: pale seamless walls with honest seams, one long low window onto black space, a single shut bound volume on the desk, nothing else. Soft even light from concealed recessed sources. Muted grey, soft brown, one faint warm band. Photographed, not rendered: real skin with moisture and fine texture, high-ISO grain heavier in the shadows, a long lens with shallow depth of field, slight softness toward the corners, a touch under-exposed, muted natural colour. ### 5c. Outstanding lore illustrations — the 7 October 2026 audit (10 generated, 2 own frames, 3 cards)

Written 7 October 2026 under the rule recorded the same day (*Which pages
carry an image*, above): a place, a people, a thing or a sky gets an
illustration. All **16:9 landscape**, all present-day unless the page says
otherwise, every negative inside the blockquote. Two pages take Dermot's own
frames as they are and three institutions take emblem cards; those five have
no prompt here and are recorded under the intake of the same date. Photo-first
where a camera could have taken it: the references are his frames, sent as
image parts, for light and weather and never for content.

- **`greenward-habitat.jpg`** — *a single ring in a high circular orbit, holding two hundred and forty people, most of whom will never set foot on the world beneath them.*
  The anchor is the non-descent clause made visible: the ring and the world in one frame, and nothing between them. No surface detail that could be read as a landing site; the world is a green disc with weather on it and the ring is small against it.
  > Documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, from a survey craft holding station a few kilometres off, available light, 16:9 landscape, muted natural colour, still, slightly too empty: Greenward, a single-ring habitat for two hundred and forty people in a high circular orbit, eight thousand kilometres above a living green world. The ring is about three hundred and fifty metres across, a plain matte grey composite torus with honest panel seams, patched in a few greys, no markings, no window band, nothing lit, turning slowly (about two turns a minute, so it reads as still). Four thin straight spokes join it to a small non-rotating hub at its centre. The hub's axis points at the sun: on its sunward face a single flat dark disc of solar collectors, and from its shaded side four thin flat radiator panels stand straight out along the axis, edge-on to the sun so they show as lines. At the far end of the hub, one plain closed docking port, round and flush, with nothing docked at it. The sun lights the whole station from one side, so one face of the ring is bright and the rest is in its own shadow. Below and beyond, the planet fills the lower half of the frame as a curved limb with cloud bands and a pale ocean, no city lights and nothing built on it; the ring is small and exact against it, and the gulf between them is the subject. Deep black above. Photographed, not rendered: a real lens, slight softness toward the corners, fine high-ISO grain in the black, a touch under-exposed. Negative: solar panels on the ring or on the spokes, panels inside the ring, wings of solar panels, a lit flank, window band, glowing windows, running lights, engine glow, spaceship, shuttle, landing craft, docking arm, anything docked, tether, cable to the ground, space elevator, sleek hull, fins, antenna forest, painted name, lens flare, nebula, large rendered stars, sci-fi gloss; readable text, lettering, numerals, signage, labels, branding or written characters of any script anywhere in frame; holograms, projected light; weapons. Render negatives: 3D render, CGI, octane render, video-game render, concept art, plastic sheen, over-smooth surfaces. Landscape orientation.

The 19 August prompt named none of sheet D's figures and asked for "no docking structure", while sheet D gives a hub with docking and spokes. Now written to the sheet: a 350 m ring for 240 people at about two turns a minute, four spokes, a non-rotating hub whose axis points at the sun, collectors on its sunward face, radiators edge-on from its shaded side, and one closed docking port with nothing at it. The non-descent clause is kept by having nothing docked, no landing craft and nothing joining it to the ground. A docking port is for orbit and says nothing about going down.)*

The orbit is high, so Earth is a disc behind the habitat and does not fill the frame. The camera's imperfection is the port it was taken through.

liquid methane, so all three are generated; one of Dermot's still-water
frames is sent with the Stillwater prompt for the look of dark flat water and
nothing else. Three entries under a heading `scripts/image-prompts.js` reads,
so `--generate --only titan,ligeia-habitat,stillwater-station` reaches them.
Generation is a desktop step (his key); the prompts are the record until
then. Ligeia's figures are derived on sheet H of `starship-design.md`,

What is true of Titan and binds all three, from the planet page and the
science behind it: noon is a dim orange twilight under an unbroken
hydrocarbon haze, with the sun about a hundredth as bright as at Earth and
rarely visible as a disc; the ground is water ice as hard as stone, strewn
with dark organic grain; methane and ethane are the liquids, falling as
large slow drops and lying in seas near the north pole so calm they are
flat to within millimetres; nobody outside wears a pressure suit, since the
air stands at one and a half atmospheres, but everyone wears heavy
insulation and breathes air they brought; **Saturn is not seen from the
surface** through that haze, so a ringed planet in a Titan sky is the
generator's cliché and fails, however handsome; and from orbit Saturn may
appear, but with its rings **edge-on**, a thin line through the globe, since
Titan orbits in Saturn's ring plane. Nothing joins the ring to the ground.

### 5i. Outstanding lore illustrations — 15 October 2026 (Callisto Station, from the lore page)

A fourth Locations page with no image, written the same day as the three
above and after them: `src/lore/callisto-station.md`, a station, and a place
gets an illustration. Its own section rather than a fourth entry under § 5h,
because that heading names its three pages and this one is not a Titan page;
the heading here is one `scripts/image-prompts.js` reads, so
`--generate --only callisto-station` reaches it. Every visual fact is from
the page or from what is known of Callisto itself; where the page is silent
the prompt takes the plainest hard-SF reading and the entry names it as the
prompt's choice. No camera of ours has stood on Callisto and nothing in
`own-photography.json` is a cratered ice plain under a black sky, so it is
generated, with no reference sent. Generation is a desktop step (his key);
the prompt is the record until then. It takes no sheet in
`starship-design.md`: a station dug into ice is not a hull, as Stillwater
was not, and the note on sheet H says so.

What is true of Callisto and binds the frame, from the page and the science
behind it: it is *a battered ball of ice and rock with next to no atmosphere*,
so the sky is black by day, there is no haze, no fog and no blue, and every
shadow is hard with no fill; the surface is ancient and saturated with
craters, dark dusty ice and rock with bright clean ice on crater rims and
peaks; the sun is small and harsh at about four percent of Earth's daylight;
Callisto keeps one face to Jupiter and the station stands on that face, so
Jupiter *hangs in the black sky over the surface hatches, about eight times
the width of a full Moon seen from Earth, and never rises or sets*, about
four degrees across, banded cream, tan and rust, and its faint rings are
not visible to the eye; the station is dug in, *metres of ice are the
cheapest shielding there is*, so very little shows at the surface; it was
an Imperium patrol post and is a Survey Corps post now, with nothing
military on it and no weapon anywhere. **Unlike Titan, anyone outside here
is in a pressure suit**: there is no air to stand in, so the Titan rule
(insulation, a mask, no hard helmet) inverts, and the suit is the uniform.
The rank page says the field shell *is a pressure liner first and a garment
second*, that the Survey Corps' shell is deep olive, and that its tabs are
shapes read *through a visor*; so a surveyor on Callisto's surface wears a
deep olive pressure shell with a close helmet, and her marks are one or two
small plain geometric tabs, never a word, never a flag.

- **`callisto-station.jpg`** — *Ligeia is a station that became a home. Callisto is one that never did, and was never meant to.*
  The surface in the long local afternoon, from the ground, with Jupiter fixed above it as the page's last paragraph wants: the thing nobody stops noticing. What the station shows above the ice is the page's *surface hatches* and the *buoy cradles* of *Life on One*: low smooth mounds of ice shielding over the buried modules, a few flush sealed hatches, and one open-sided shelter with a cradle under it holding a long-baseline buoy, which the Navigation Corps page has already pictured as a small plain unmarked cylinder, so it keeps that shape. Two surveyors at the cradle in olive pressure shells, small, backs turned. Prompt's choices, the page being silent: the station stands well off the sub-Jovian point, so Jupiter sits about a third of the way up the sky rather than at the zenith, which is what lets one frame hold the ground and the planet; the sun low behind the camera's right shoulder, about 120° of sky away from the planet, so **Jupiter is gibbous, about three-quarters lit on its right-hand side with a soft curved terminator on the left**, which is the phase that geometry gives and the one the generator's full-disc Jupiter fails; three flat dark radiator slabs standing on edge on the ice a little way off, the fusion plant's heat with nowhere else to go (principle 8, derived, his to strike); no survey craft on a pad, since the page has them away for months and no sheet has given them a shape (sheet E's lesson: put as a choice before any picture); the two figures and the sealed hatches as the hints of the century, either of which may carry the frame alone. No faces, so no heritage to choose.

The sun is small and hard, low in the sky behind the camera's right shoulder and out of frame, so every shadow is long, sharp-edged and completely black with no fill, running away from the camera to the left, and the light is thin and harsh, like a bright winter afternoon that has had most of its light taken away. ### 5j. Outstanding lore illustrations — 15 October 2026 (Stillwater's First Hall, an inline interior from the lore page)

A second image for `src/lore/stillwater-station.md`, later the same day as
its lead image in § 5h: an **inline illustration for the page body**, the
way the Prismere and Tír na nÓg pages carry one under the paragraph it
draws, not a replacement for the exterior. The page's `image:` stays the
§ 5h frame; this one goes under the first paragraph of *The First Hall* as
`![…](/star-rangers/images/lore/stillwater-first-hall.jpg)`, named
`<page>-<subject>` as the Prismere set is, filed flat under `lore/` at
1600 px. Its own section so the parser reads it and
`--generate --only stillwater-first-hall` reaches it alone; no reference is
sent, since nothing in `own-photography.json` is a sealed module's inside and
the § 5h water frame has nothing to give a room. No sheet in
`starship-design.md`: sheet H's note already says Stillwater is a surface
station and takes none, and a room inside it is further still from a hull.
Generation is a desktop step (his key); the prompt is the record until then.

What the page fixes, and binds the frame: the Hall is *the station's first
landed module*, set down in the 2130s CE, standing *at the centre of the
oldest section, heated and sealed and not used for anything*; it holds the
Authority's founding charter *in its original enrolment*, kept whole with
every amendment enrolled beside it; it *is not a shrine, and the Authority's
register is careful not to describe it as one*; new crews are *walked
through it on their first rotation down*. The station is *insulated rather
than pressurised*, built around *methane seeping in from the ground into
air that will burn*, and its oldest sections have been *resealed more times
than anyone on the current crew could list*, each resealing recorded; the
Titan page makes station safety *chiefly a matter of seals and gas
monitors*. So the picture is the oldest working room of a cryogenic
station, kept clean and kept plainly, and never a place of veneration: no
altar arrangement, no candles, no reverent lighting, no relic case, no
stained glass, no plaque. The enrolment itself cannot be shown open, since
a generator cannot spell and an open founding is an object whose purpose is
to carry writing (*The lettering ban cannot beat the scene*, above), so it
is **closed**: a sealed archival case lying on a plain shelf, the
convention's own sanctioned substitute, and nothing legible anywhere.

- **`stillwater-first-hall.jpg`** — *The Hall is not a shrine, and the Authority's register is careful not to describe it as one.*
  The room from its threshold, with one crew member standing in the hatchway from behind, as a new crew is walked through on a first rotation down; the camera is behind their shoulder in the short link, so the figure is small to one side of the frame and the room is the subject. ### 5k. Outstanding lore illustrations — 15 October 2026 (Titan's surface from orbit, an inline near-infrared frame for the planet page)

A second image for `src/lore/planets/titan.md`, later the same day as its
lead image in § 5h: an **inline illustration for the page body**, on the
§ 5j and Prismere precedent, not a replacement for the surface frame. The
page's `image:` stays the § 5h ground-level frame; this one goes under the
haze paragraph of *The World* as
`![…](/star-rangers/images/lore/titan-from-orbit.jpg)`, named
`<page>-<subject>` and filed flat under `lore/` at 1600 px, as the Prismere
page's inline frames are though the page sits under `planets/`. Its own
section so the parser reads it and `--generate --only titan-from-orbit`
reaches it alone; no reference is sent, since nothing in
`own-photography.json` is a world seen from orbit. No sheet in
`starship-design.md`: the craft the camera is mounted on is not in frame.
Generation is a desktop step (his key); the prompt is the record until then.

**Why this frame is infrared, and why it is grey.** In visible light Titan's
surface cannot be seen from orbit at all: the hydrocarbon haze the page
describes is unbroken, and what a camera records is the featureless orange
ball that the § 5h Ligeia prompt draws on purpose. The surface shows only
through a handful of narrow windows in the near infrared where methane does
not absorb (near 0.94, 1.08, 1.28, 1.6, 2.0 and 5 microns), and by radar;
that is how the first orbiter mapped it, and a 29th-century survey camera
has no other way either, since optics are optics (*Hard science fiction by
default*). A frame taken through one window is a frame in one band, so it
is **monochrome**: a neutral grey image the way any single-filter frame is,
never a false-colour composite, which is a map product and not a photograph
anybody took. Even in a window the light scatters through the haze both
ways, so the surface comes back **softened**, every edge diffuse, and that
softness is physically right and is kept; a crisp surface would be the
generator's Moon. This entry takes the **2-micron window**, the one that
shows the surface most cleanly against the haze, and says so here and in the
prompt's description, with nothing written in the image.

What is true of Titan from orbit and binds the frame, from the page and the
science behind it: the dark low dunes of frozen organic grain *girdle the
equator* (the page's own words), and in a window they are the darkest ground
on the disc, broad dark belts wrapping the equator; against them, on one
side of the disc, stands one large bright irregular region straddling the
equator, the brightest ground on Titan (Xanadu); the mid-latitudes are
mottled paler plains; the polar seas lie around the north pole and are
the darkest things of all, **and the record's own year puts them at the edge of the light** (Opus
review, same day, correcting a CE/UCSD slip in the first draft, which
dated the frame to 2826 CE and so found the north in midwinter). 2826 UCSD
is 2626 CE. By Titan's real seasons (a northern winter solstice in 2032 CE
and a Saturn year of about 29.46 Earth years) 2626 CE falls about five
years after a northern winter solstice and two before the spring equinox:
the sun stands about thirteen to fourteen degrees south of Titan's equator,
and polar night covers only the cap north of about 76° N. So Ligeia Mare,
at about 79° N, is still in the dark, which is § 5h's Stillwater winter,
late in it rather than deep; and the southern reaches of Kraken Mare, the
largest sea, lie just inside the lit disc under a very low sun. The top of
the frame therefore shows the lit mid-latitudes running up into a broad
dark irregular sea near the terminator, with the terminator and the black
polar cap beyond it. A sun glint is still left out: with the sun that far
south and the camera looking down on the lit face, the mirror point falls
on land, not on a sea.
The limb carries a thin pale soft rim where the detached haze forward-scatters
the sunlight, brighter than the surface beneath it. Saturn is out of frame
(from high Titan orbit it would be small with its rings edge-on, as § 5h has
it; the disc of Titan fills this frame and needs no second body). Ligeia is
not in frame: a habitat is a visible-light object and this is a window frame.
Nothing joins the surface to orbit.

  The world from high orbit as only a window camera can see it: a survey camera on a hull mount, filtered to the 2-micron window, looking down on the lit face with the disc filling most of the frame and the night side cut off at the top. The page is the authority for what is on the ground (the dunes girdling the equator, the seas around the north pole, the unbroken haze, Saturn unseen from below); the science of the windows is the authority for how it looks (grey, soft, the dunes dark, Xanadu bright, the limb rimmed). Prompt's choices, the page being silent: the 2-micron window over the others; a hull-mounted survey camera on a craft in high orbit rather than a hand camera through a port, so there is no port edge and the frame is square to the disc; the disc placed with its equator across the lower-middle of the frame so the bright region, the dune belts and the terminator all fit; the northern terminator shown and the seas not, which is the year's and not a taste; no Saturn and no craft, since the frame is the disc; the camera as the century's hint on its own, which the audit's (A) allows for a frame with nothing made in it but what it looks at.

The whole image is neutral grey, a single-band photograph with no colour anywhere in it: pale greys, mid greys, dark greys and black, like a fine-grained black-and-white frame. ### 5l. Outstanding lore illustrations — 16 October 2026 (Tsittak, from the lore page)

A new Locations page with no image: `src/lore/tsittak.md`, a settlement, and a
place gets an illustration. Written by Opus under the 16 October rule in
`CLAUDE.md` (a prompt whose content is mostly physics, geometry or dates is
Opus's), since what decides this frame is where the light comes from. The
heading is one `scripts/image-prompts.js` reads, so
`--generate --only tsittak` reaches it. No camera of ours has been to deep
interstellar space and nothing in `own-photography.json` is a metal body under
a full field of stars, so it is generated, with no reference sent. It takes no
sheet in `starship-design.md`: the body is a settlement cut into rock, not a
hull, as Stillwater and Callisto were not, and the camera's vessel is not in
frame.

What is true of Tsittak and binds the frame, from the page and the physics
behind it: it is cut into *a lone body of nickel-iron, a few kilometres
across*, drifting *with no star within several light-years*, so **no sun lights
it**. The only light on the body is its own, and the page is exact about how
little that is: *seen from outside, it is a dark body with a lit dock and
almost nothing else.* With no sun and no air, the sky is not black the way
Callisto's is: the camera's exposure is set for a dim lit dock, so the whole
sky behind the body is a dense field of stars and the faint band of the galaxy,
sharp points with no twinkle, no haze and no glow. The body reads mostly as a
**silhouette against the stars**, its outline found where it hides them, with
the dock's light picking out only the cut faces near it. Chthonari building is
subtractive (*the members are left, not built*), so the dock is a recess cut
into the metal, its edges smooth and deliberate, with nothing bolted on:
no masts, no antennae, no gantries, no superstructure. The quiet-zone tunnel
has **no visible form at all**; the page and the Lagrange page both say there
is nothing to see or survey until a vessel is inside it, so the frame shows
none. No person is in frame: the Chthonari are inside the rock.

what binds it is on the page: an old orange dwarf, so warm, low-contrast light;
high, old, dry uplands of plateau and broad valley far from small shallow seas;
low, long-lived producers that can stand grey for decades in a dry spell; no
Mnemari in frame unless the portrait's body section is followed, and no human
settlement. Generation is a desktop step.

### 6. Images that should not stay — audited 2026-08-10

Open work 1 and 5 are the images that are **missing**. This is the other half:
images that **exist and shouldn't**. Prompted by Dermot noticing that Saint

> below stands as the record of why it was done; the counts do not.

**The corpus carries two visual languages.** Alt-text length is a reliable
tell for which images were ever actually looked at, and it comes out bimodal:

old book"*, *"Computer circuit board close-up"* — and 40 sit at 120+ with real

because that is what they are. Roughly **55% of the 120 illustrated lore and
character pages** are contemporary stock photography, against a house style
that says in so many words: *not contemporary glamour or lifestyle shoots.*

Crossing) — the portfolio's *Dalkey Island*, unmodified from the 1600px site

also include places that local fans would recognise. I am ok with that."*
So a candidate from his portfolio is never rejected merely because a local
reader could name the place — the record is filmed on location. What still
disqualifies is unchanged: structures the setting cannot absorb (the
Garachico summit cross), anachronisms, recognisable people, and anything
that *names* the place in frame (signage, lettering). The distinction from

non-local reader can import.

(no night skies), Where the Weather Stops (no caves), or Quern's storm

**Method, stated so a later audit knows what to trust:** six images were
opened and read. The 66-page cohort is *inferred from caption style* and is
not individually confirmed. Confirming it is its own pass — and per this
file's own standing warning, it must be done by opening files, not by
reasoning about filenames or alt strings.

#### Triage: sort by what the image is doing, not by where it came from

"Replace all the stock" is the wrong unit — it counts 66 images when the
number that matters is nearer 25, and it would replace things worth keeping.

**Tier 1 — photographs of real people standing in for characters. These must
go.** The only non-negotiable tier, for a reason that is not about house
style: a generated portrait of an invented person claims nothing, but a
photograph of a real stranger captioned as a character makes a claim about an
actual human being, and a false one. `dagny-voss.jpg` is a real woman
presented as an orbital refinery director on Aspenar. That is testimony
pointed at the wrong person — the same fraud the photography site's absolute
rule exists to prevent, running in the other direction. There is also a
licensing question worth *checking rather than assuming*: stock model
releases commonly restrict portraying a model as a fictional person or
implying endorsement, and these publish on owned domains under
`CONTENT-LICENSE.md`. **Roughly 15–20 portraits. Do these first.**

**Tier 2 — stock photographs standing in for specific invented places and
institutions. Should go.** An empty Earth parliament chamber as the Star
Rangers command hierarchy; a Mediterranean archway as Cill Aoife. Wrong in a
way a reader can point at. **Roughly 10–15.**
**Policy settled 3 September 2026** by the exemption statement under
*Conventions*: a stock landscape is replaced from Dermot's archive when a frame
fits and carded when none does, opportunistically, never regenerated from a
prompt. No wholesale pass; the tier closes as each page is next touched.

**Tier 3 — Dermot's own photography. Keep it, and lean on it much harder.**
A real Irish upland standing in for an alien world claims nothing false
because it names nothing: a real place, unnamed, his own work, no model
release in sight. **The unpublished photo backlog is a lore-art resource** —
Kenya, Tenerife, Scandinavia and Irish material sitting on `F:` includes
acacias in dust, a drowned forest, flamingos, volcanic strata, a cloud sea.
That is alien terrain already, and `earth-leopard-grassland.jpg` shows the
practice is established. For any lore entry about landscape, weather, flora
or fauna, the archive beats a prompt: cheaper, better, and it moves the
corpus toward his own work rather than away from it.

**Tier 4 — abstract and texture stock. Lowest priority; probably keep.**
Star fields, light gradients, circuit boards, nebulae. No person, no place,
no claim, and nobody's reading is broken by them. Replace opportunistically
when already in the file, never as a project. **Roughly half the 66.**

So the real work is **25–30 images**, not 66 — and a good share of those
should come from the camera rather than a prompt.

### Intake 2026-09-05 — the shadow's two costumes, parked

Dermot supplied two generated stills and a 25-second clip (Grok; no prompt
kept) with the direction in `intake-2026-09-05.md` — a shadow wearing
Tissadelle's appearance at the edge of Tobble's universe. Parked, nothing
ships: `story-bible/reference-art/tissadelle-shadow-1-2026-09-05.jpg`,
`tissadelle-shadow-2-2026-09-05.jpg` (1152×1728), and the clip as a
five-frame strip, `tissadelle-shadow-video-frames-2026-09-05.jpg` — the
14 MB source file was **not** committed, on the ground that reference
material does not need to ride into every production clone; Dermot holds
the original.

**What they show:** the stills — a red-haired woman, hair worn long and
loose and dressed with metal, in knotwork and jewellery and a dress cut to
be looked at, against a glowing Celtic knot and circuitry. The clip — the
same woman in a navy high-collared coat with gold stars and leaf-work on the
cloth, cut short over bare legs and boots, walking a candlelit chamber for
the camera.

**How the draft reads them:** as the *shadow's* costumes and not as hers.
The character page has her always formally dressed and never dressed to be
looked at; the hair on her portrait is tied back; and *Reading Rank at a
Glance* (4 September) puts rank on a plain tab and never on the garment. So
each image is a tell — surface got right by something that cannot tell what
the surface is for — and `scene-draft-youre-up-early.md` uses them that way
without describing either garment beyond the finding.

**Why parked rather than filed:** they depict a thing whose nature is
undecided (three shapes in the intake); the tone rule and the no-sexualised-
content rule make a published image of the shadow not obviously yes; and
the scene they belong to sits behind an unpublished terminus. If one ever
ships, the honest shape is the same as the headmate's — an in-world
artist's impression, prospective only — and it would need a clean re-make
at size, since neither still is the portrait floor and the clip is 768 px.

### Intake 2026-09-18 — strength and courage: five illustrations, none filed

Dermot supplied one generated still and four generated clips (Grok era by

  and backdrop, holding a plank and doing push-ups with a leg raised, to

- **Clip dated 11 May 2026**, 30 s, 448×672. **Byte-identical to
  `src/video/grok-video-2026-05-10.mp4`**, the orphan `video-prompts.md` has
  tracked since 20 August — now identified there. Red hair long and loose, a
  fitted navy-and-silver costume uniform with a spiral badge and
  lettering-like marks, heels, at a starship viewport over a nebula, speaking
  or singing to camera: the earliest Grok-era Tissadelle, in the costume
  uniform the 5 September regeneration replaced.
- **Clip dated 7 July 2026**, 30 s, 448×672, with audio. The same face, hair
  loose, in a glossy red two-piece, posing and flexing on a present-day night
  street under illuminated signs, some readable and one naming a real city.
  Not in either repository.
- **Clip dated 2 July 2026**, 30 s, 448×672. A black leather halter minidress
  with knotwork trim, barefoot, walking through a field of drifting rocks
  under a red nebula, a crowd of seated harpists behind. Not in either

**How the intake reads them:** the still and the 13 September clip picture
the direction — strength as a body at exercise — and are to-camera, in a
studio, which is a presentation and not a Ranger at work, so neither could
stand as a portrait under the guardrails above (*outwardly plain*, *nothing
in the image invites the viewer*). The 2 July and 7 July clips are the
register the 5 September intake assigned to the shadow at the edge — hair
loose and dressed with metal, knotwork, *a dress cut to be looked at* — and
are read the same way: not her. The 7 July clip also carries readable
signage naming a real city, the *formation-of-star-rangers.jpg* failure in
motion.

**Why nothing is parked:** the still is the private repository's already;
the orphan is in `src/video/` already; and the three clips that are in
neither repository were put to Dermot as a choice (nowhere here, a frame
strip each in `reference-art/`, or the private repository in its own
session) rather than parked by default — `intake-2026-09-18.md`, *Left
open*, B. The degree of strength the page states is choice A there; the
recommended and drafted degree needs no image.

**Decent and modest enough for a public repo?** — Dermot's question the same
session, answered in the intake's addendum: decent as a file in a public
repository, yes; modest enough for *this* site as a picture of *her*, no, on
the 4 September any-age principle (the deep neckline), her page's *never
dressed to be looked at*, and the portrait guardrails' *nothing invites the
viewer*; and moot for filing, since it is the private repository's file. A
re-make through the pipeline — high-necked, at work, attention off-frame — is
the shape that would clear every bar.

**Ruled by Dermot the same day, verbatim *Recommendations accepted*:** the
drafted degree stands and no image is re-made; the three unfiled clips stay
with him; the orphan stays until the video note's question is ruled — **and
then removed later the same day at his instruction** (*Remove the orphan
video from src/video*), deleted rather than parked.

### 7. Codex art — in-world artists' impressions

The pool the 18 August rule created, first filled 3 September 2026. Entries
here are **body images** for codex entries: the entry's `image:` stays a
designed card (`make-codex-cover.ps1`, usually with the artwork as
`-Underlay`), and the artwork itself is shown inline in the body with a caption
naming its in-world maker or provenance. `scripts/image-prompts.js` files these
under `src/images/codex/`. Dermot's ruling of 3 September on the first case:
*in-world artist's impression, no watermarks or overlaid text.*

- **`asteria-the-sage-impression-artwork.jpg`** — the parked headmate image
  (Intake 2026-08-24 above), re-made clean at size. Dermot's own supplied
  picture is the reference; the prompt asks for a *painting* rather than a
  photograph, because the entry presents it as an artist's impression made from
  a description and not from a sitting, and a painterly surface says that
  without a caption. It also puts distance between this image and the
  character-portrait house style, which is the point: this is not a portrait
  of a character, it is a picture somebody in the world made of a person they
  were told about. Register still and watchful, hope in it, no grimness. The
  standing negative is inside the blockquote, with signatures, monograms and
  watermarks added to it, since the reference carries one.
  References: `story-bible/reference-art/tissadelle-headmate-2026-08-24.jpg`
  > A painted portrait in the manner of an artist's impression made from a description rather than a sitting: a woman who appears in her thirties, pale, with loose blue hair and pale blue eyes, in a black hooded cloak worked with fine silver botanical embroidery over dark layered clothing with a belt, standing among bare winter branches at night, three-quarter turn, level gaze past the viewer, still and watchful. Visible brushwork and a limited palette of night blue, black and silver; the branches thin and dissolve into the dark at the edges of the picture as if the painter stopped where the description ran out. Quiet, composed, a little hopeful rather than grim. No readable text, lettering, numerals, signature, monogram, watermark, logo, signage, labels, branding or written characters of any script anywhere in frame; no holograms, projected light, glowing displays, screens, monitors or consoles; no visible lamp, light fitting or bulb; no flat studio backdrop, gradient background, glamour lighting, corporate headshot or posed smiling to camera; no weapons; no drawn frame or border around the picture. 16:9 landscape.

## History (2026-07-24)

A full visual review of ~250 files in July 2026 found five character portraits
with flatly wrong content, a Vedic astrological chart standing in for a star
atlas, a broken codex cover, and a set of quality issues. All of the
wrong-content items are now fixed.

**Replaced from Firefly generations** (alt text rewritten on each):
`ilse-korvain` (US Army stock photo → Imperium cyber-revenant; v2 after v1
tipped into body horror), `aldera` (`.png` fantasy forest → a tabby matching her
own gallery field-photos), `maren-solveig-krast` (contemporary policewoman →
archival general's portrait), `karla-wender` (corporate headshot labelled
"engineer" → a pilot at the helm), `orla-shepherd` (office businesswoman →
upland flockholder), `qiren-tal` (dark-fantasy monster → basalt-sheen insectoid
engineer, from Dermot's own reworked prompt), `rook-7` (too sleek → aging
retrofit chassis; v2 after v1 arrived furnished with the NYPD), `nessa`
(purebred studio photo → wind-matted cat on barnacled rock), `lore/cerebraun`
(grey-alien bust → architectural indirection), `hero/atlas-chart`,
`hero/s01e01-corridor`, plus a `lore/five-layers` upgrade to a layered-planes
galaxy. `codex/cosmic-limitation-on-evil.jpg` was rebuilt with the cover
generator (dissolution ring, `CONTESTED` stamp from the paper's own status).

**Two corrections to the audit itself**, both worth remembering:

1. The reported "three-way lore image shuffle" was a **false positive**. All
   three files (`five-layers`, `formation-of-star-rangers`,
   `frontier-transformation-protocols`) already matched their own alt text on
   inspection, and git confirmed none had been touched since 2026-07-13 — so
   nothing was ever shuffled, and no fourth image was missing.
2. The `cerebraun` target was mis-named: the grey-alien bust was on
   `lore/cerebraun.jpg` (the **species** entry), not
   `lore/cerebraun-hegemony.jpg`, which is an on-template designed cover for the
   **polity** entry and was correctly left alone.

## Meta-page heroes (2026-07-25)

The out-of-character section — `/story-engine/` and the Journal index under it —
now has heroes of its own, both chosen from a set of eight generated candidates.
Three pages (About, Journal, Story Engine) had been opening with the same
`hero/about-writer.jpg`; About keeps it, the other two no longer share it.

- **`hero/story-engine.jpg`** — a brass machine whose riveted nameplate reads
  *Story Engine*, gears below, steam rising. On `/story-engine/`. Whimsical
  brass on a hard-SF site is deliberate and confined to the out-of-character
  section; nothing in-universe uses it.
- **`hero/journal-notebook.jpg`** — an open journal headed *Author's Journal*
  above a handwritten dated entry. On the Journal index.

**Selecting a text-bearing generation.** Six of the eight candidates were
rejected on lettering, which is the same failure the codex-cover generator
exists to avoid — an image model cannot spell, so the only safe pick is one
where every legible word is short and correct. Rejected: a gear array labelled
`PLOT / CHARACTER / SETTING / CONFLICT` that labelled two different gears
`PLOT`; a printing press whose scroll read `bd what...` and dissolved into
gibberish at the bottom; a journal quoting a named real author (attribution the
site would then be making in a decorative image) and hard-dating itself to 2024;
a journal spread carrying a pencil-sketched face, which reads as a specific
character on a page that is explicitly *not* in-universe. The two winners each
carry one short correctly-spelled phrase and nothing else legible.

**Cropping portrait generations for `.page-hero-image`.** Heroes render at
`width: 100%; height: 320px; object-fit: cover` in an 1100px column — roughly
3.4:1 — so CSS keeps only the middle band of whatever it is given. Both sources
were 768×1152 portraits; each was cropped to 16:9 around a chosen centre and
upscaled to 1600×900, with the centre picked so that the CSS band lands on the
lettering (verified by simulating the 1100×320 crop before committing, not
after). A naive centre crop put the nameplate and the journal's title outside
the visible band on both. Worth repeating for any portrait-orientation source.

### Intake 2026-10-07 — the finish, and which pages carry an image

Dermot's question the same day: *"check for new images needed or missing
images on the star-rangers repo"*, then the rule above on which pages carry
one. Counted from `main` at 709eea7a: 52 lore entries pending in this file's
manifest (prompts written, generation the bottleneck); 23 lore pages and 12
character pages with neither an image nor an entry here; two stamped
placeholder cards still live (the About the Author and Characters heroes); no
page references a file that is absent. Read by his rule:

**Lore pages that get an image** (prompts to write; photo-first where a camera
could have taken it, from `own-photography.json`): *Greenward* and *The Guest
Ring* (habitats, generated); *New Cotswolds* and *Winterbourne* (settled
country, his own landscape frames as plates); *Quern* (a planet, generated);
*The Ilveth* (a people, generated); *The Tally* (a people and their ark,
generated, or an emblem card); *The Eden Bureau Uniform* (a garment on a
figure at work, generated); *The Honest Dark* (a night sky, his own frame);
*The Thin Inheritance* (soil, his own close frame); *Weather on Other Worlds*
(a sky, his own storm frame); *Where the Weather Stops* (a cave, his own frame
if one exists, else none); *The Star Rangers Music Corps*, *The Star Rangers
Survey Corps* and *The Archive* (institutions, emblem cards by
`make-emblem-card.ps1`).

**Lore pages that stay bare** (abstract concepts, doctrine, law): *Climate
Repair and the Origin of Terraforming*, *Commissioned Standing*, *Habitable,
for Whom*, *Habitats and the Worlds Beneath Them*, *Performers and Generated
Work*, *The Enrolled Text*, *The Ladder in Other Tongues*, *The Shape of a
Life*. *Habitable, for Whom* is a Physics page and may take an inline diagram.

**Characters that get a portrait** (a body the record describes): Ariel Pinya,
Bram Tollick, Ilsabet Corren, Ingrid Halvorsen, Odile Ferrant, Oriel Fenwick,
Tomas Brennock, Wren of Knight Pellam (human); Toval (Krenyi, Syra's portrait
as the kind's reference); Stone-First and Went-Round (Pandoid, Teddy's
portrait as the kind's reference, *more like a panda*).

**Character that stays bare:** The Kept Line, a Dragon known only from
instrument logs.

The entries for the 20 generated images are written: lore under *5c* and
portraits under *8* in *Open work*. Dermot's word on the spend the same day
(*"Cost of image generation should be ok"*), and the run started the same hour.
Ariel Pinya came off the portrait list on reading her page, which says the
record holds no portrait of her; she stays bare by her own page.

### 10. Missing portraits — the seven founding viewpoints (queued 10 October 2026)

Dermot's direction, verbatim: *"Run the seven missing portraits"*, the day
after the seven character pages for the POV ids that had none (PR #1050).
Each is a person with a body, so each gets a portrait under the 7 October
rule. All **16:9 landscape**, filed through `import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200`
with the finish at strength 1. The 28 July guardrails and the modesty bar
inside every blockquote: at work, attention off-frame, nothing that invites
the viewer, no lettering, no period technology. Heritage is not in the record
and not in the prompt; gender is the record's; age only where the record
implies it. Six are the founding era, 2712 to 2723 UCSD, under the
old-fashioned hint: an earlier century than the record's present, with the
Military Space Command's severe service dress where the page wears it
(`sildron-drey.jpg` is the precedent). The seventh is a Science Corps
Principal in 2814, under the Ranger block.

  Eden's chief scientist at twenty to four in the morning, station time, the moment she signs the model over and does not go to the docking ring. The habitat is a working interior, not a laboratory set.

### 16. Missing portraits — Tobble, the first non-physical member (written 14 October 2026, Fable)

Dermot's rulings of 14 October 2026 (`intake-2026-10-14.md`), verbatim:
*"Non-physical headmates get fantasy-style codex art portraits instead of the
photorealistic portraits for the host body of the plural system"*, and, on the
register, *"I do like the whimsical fantasy dress styles and lighting as shown
in the codex art portrait of Asteria the Sage"*. Tobble's page landed the same
day (`src/characters/tobble.md`, PR #1223) with no `image:`. He has no body of
his own for a camera to take, so his portrait is a **painting**, made as
Asteria's was (§ 7 above): an impression from the system's own description,
never from a sitting, with the edges dissolving where the description ran out.
It is a companion piece to `codex/asteria-the-sage-impression-artwork.jpg` by
the same kind of practice, and that painting is passed as a reference for its
medium, palette and handling only. It is a character portrait, so it is
**16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 for the slot, through `import-image.ps1
-MaxEdge 1200` at **finish strength 0**: it is a painting, not a photograph,
and the photographic finish is for photographs.

What the record holds of him, and all the prompt draws on: a ginger cat, he/him,
a person and not an animal (`tobble.md`, `plural-minds.md`); the deeper layer
he keeps, *kept records, checked procedure, arithmetic done twice*; and the
Dock Seven block of S05E02C03, where what went in was *a hillside, and a low
stone wall with the third course shifted … and the particular gold of a home
star*, and it *came up grey, and then gold*, and he *sat down in the middle of
it, being a cat, and waited to see what it would do*. The painting takes that
moment and nothing beyond it. Choices made, each Dermot's to overrule and none
written to the page:

- **He wears one garment** *(revised 14 October 2026, the same evening, at
  Dermot's word on the filed frame, verbatim: "Yes something that makes Tobble
  look like a person in the shape of a cat, or slightly similar to the Smart
  Pets", overruling the first filing's choice that he wears nothing)*. A short
  mantle across the shoulders in night blue with silver botanical embroidery,
  closed at the throat with one plain clasp: a person's garment and a
  companion to Asteria's cloak. Its low standing collar sits where a certified
  Smart Pet collar sits (`smart-pet.md`: *a collar that looks like a collar:
  matte, closed, without a light*), so the resemblance is one a stranger could
  make and be wrong about, which is the misreading his page records. No tag,
  bell, buckle or lead, since those make him somebody's animal; no hat, boots,
  belt or sword, since those make him the costumed animal of the Puss-in-Boots
  trope, which the trope default refuses. Body and posture stay wholly a cat's.
  The first filing, with nothing worn, is kept in `image-out/` and recorded in
  `image-prompts.md`.
- **He sits as a person sits**, upright on the wall he chose, forepaws
  together, head level, a steady gaze past the viewer, the bearing of a
  colleague. Not standing, not on two legs, not with hands. The 28 July
  guardrails are met the same way as Asteria's: still and watchful, not to
  camera.
- **The light is the chapter's**: the last grey before the home star, with the
  first gold on his fur and the top of the wall. The palette is limited to
  pre-dawn grey, the blue-black of the shadow side (which is where it sits
  beside Asteria's night blue), ginger and one gold.
- **The wall is the chapter's**, dry-stone, the third course shifted. Nothing
  else from the inner world is placed, since the record has not itemised it.
- **Century:** nothing made is in frame but the wall, and an unmortared field
  wall dates no century; the frame is inside a mind in any case, where the
  13 October triage asks only that nothing present-day intrudes.

- **`tobble.jpg`** — Cat, member of Tissadelle Shepherd's plural system, the deeper layer's keeper; *because that is what I am.*
  References: `src/images/codex/asteria-the-sage-impression-artwork.jpg`
  > A painted portrait in the manner of an artist's impression made from a description rather than a sitting. The attached painting is a reference for its medium, brushwork and handling only: take nothing of its subject, figure, clothing, branches or night from it. The subject is a ginger cat, an adult of ordinary size and build, with short dense orange-ginger fur in darker tabby bands and pale amber eyes, sitting upright and composed on the flat top of a low dry-stone wall on an open hillside in the last grey before sunrise, the first gold of a rising home star touching his fur, the tips of his ears and the top course of the wall from low on one side, a little more gold than a sunrise should give, as a painter of fairy stories would paint it. He sits as a person sits who has chosen where to sit: tail laid along the stones, forepaws together, head held level and turned a little to one side, his eyes fixed on something far off beyond the edge of the picture and not on the viewer, so that the viewer sees him in three-quarter view and he does not meet the viewer's eye at all; still and watchful, the bearing of a colleague and not of anybody's pet. The wall is built without mortar, and its third course from the ground has slipped out of true along its length so the stones above sit a little proud. He wears one garment only, a person's and not a pet's: a short close-fitting mantle of dark night-blue cloth laid over his shoulders and the top of his chest, closed at the throat with a single small plain silver clasp, its edge worked with fine silver botanical embroidery of leaves and thin stems, the cloth lying flat and light so that his shape is still wholly a cat's; its low standing collar sits close and plain at the neck, matte and unadorned, where a stranger might take it at a glance for an animal's collar and be wrong. Nothing else on him. Behind him the hillside falls away in long strokes of grey-green and shadow toward a sky going from grey to gold at one edge. Heavy visible oil brushwork and a limited palette of pre-dawn grey, the deep blue-black of the shadow side, ginger and a single warm gold; the hillside and the sky thin and dissolve into bare strokes and raw ground at the edges of the picture as if the painter stopped where the description ran out. Quiet, composed, a little hopeful rather than grim. The mantle is the only garment: no hat, boots, hooded cloak, cape, sword, belt, trousers, sleeves, tunic, jacket, harness, bell, tag, pendant, medallion, buckle, strap, lead or leash, no fastening but the one clasp; not a cat-person, not standing on two legs, no human hands, no human posture, no cartoon, no caricature, no mascot, no big-eyed cuteness, no wizard's familiar, no cushion, no window, no fireside; no readable text, lettering, numerals, signature, monogram, watermark, logo, signage, labels, branding or written characters of any script anywhere in frame; no holograms, projected light, glowing displays, screens, monitors or consoles; no visible lamp, light fitting or bulb; no flat studio backdrop, gradient background, glamour lighting, posed to camera, eye contact with the viewer or looking into the camera; no weapons; no drawn frame or border around the picture. 16:9 landscape.

The record names no Earth animal for the Ovruhn and the first survey's three resemblances were the observers' (*The Thing Outsiders Get Wrong*), so the likeness rule applies at full strength: the elephant, the rhinoceros, the hippopotamus, the bull, the bear and the octopus are refused by name.

The right two-thirds of the frame is a great curved wall of dry, matte, warm grey-brown hide, finely creased and grained like living skin, rising out of the top of the frame and falling out of the bottom, low broad ridges running across it where resonant chambers lie beneath; there is no head, no face, no eye, no leg, no foot and no tail anywhere in frame. same day: none in this group is prompted, and a page that later states a
species moves its author into the ready list above.

**The fourteen sorted (16 October 2026, at Dermot's *"Yes, record the sort in
images.md § 17 and queue the five for species lines"*).** Read from the pages
themselves. Thirteen close on the same stock paragraph (*"The record gives … no
birth, no age, no species …"*), written when the authors landed on 10 October.
That paragraph lists what the record lacks; it is not a choice to withhold. So
none of the fourteen has a species *withheld*: in each case it was simply
*never stated*. The sort uses the *When the body is not relevant* clarification
in *Conventions* (#1280):

**Not a ground for bareness: self-consciousness about the body.** Dermot, the
same day, verbatim: *"for medical reasons almost all 29th century humans are
fit, healthy and no reason to feel self-conscious about their physical bodies
when clothed and posed for a portrait"*. A person is never left without a
portrait to spare them their appearance. Bareness rests only on what the record
states (the clarification above) or on a choice made inside the world (Ferren,
Ariel Pinya). The modesty bar governs how a portrait is dressed and posed, not
whether one is made.

**Ruled 16 October 2026 — the species-absent fourteen (and Halle Ostrander).**
Dermot, verbatim: *"Option A accepted"*. The choices as put: A. Keep them bare
until a page states a species, the absence marked as the record marks it
(recommended: it changes no page and follows the Halle Ostrander precedent).
B. State a species on each page first, one canon line per author, then prompt
them in batches. C. Frame each so the body's kind cannot be read: the author's
document, desk or workplace with a figure seen from behind or out of focus,
which is a portrait in name only.

### 20. Missing portraits — Ulessa, the first Mnemari the record names (written 19 October 2026, Fable; body derived the same night, prompt written the same night, Fable; generation waits on the desktop)

**Update, 19 October 2026: the body exists, and the prompt is written.**
