(*humanoid* explained as the facilities standard's word, frame Endoskelia,
not the human frame). The prompt is at the foot of this section, written on
Fable later the same night from that section and from nothing else.
Everything under *What is fixed for the prompt* stands; the first triage step
reads against the section.

Dermot's *Yes please* of 19 October 2026 to the next line of the 14 October
worklist in `open-questions.md`: a Mnemari character page and portrait
prompt. The page landed in the same PR as this entry
(`src/characters/ulessa.md`): a treaty-witness of Ilenne, requested for a
little over two centuries to Federation assembly sessions that revisit old
compacts, one of the Mnemari witnesses who raise the standing Ollune item,
present in 2826 UCSD and not Set Down. The page carries no `image:`. **This
entry writes no prompt, and says why**, under the 16 October clarification in
*Conventions* (*When the body is not relevant*) read with the 13 August ruling.

**What the record says of the body, and why it is not enough to draw.**
`src/lore/mnemari.md` (written 11 July 2026) calls the Mnemari *a sapient,
humanoid people* and *fully compatible with standard humanoid life-support*.
On 13 August 2026 Dermot ruled that the Krenyi are the only other sapient
humanoids, sharpened on 16 August to *the only other people built on the
human frame* (`species-design.md`, head); the published refusal page now
names the Mnemari among the peoples that are *genuinely otherwise* and says
*none of these is a human silhouette with features applied to it, and none
should be described, drawn or imagined as one*
(`what-the-record-refuses.md`, *Bodies and Species*); and
`cross-biosphere-taxonomy.md` files Endoskelia as humans, Krenyi and
Prismeri, with no Mnemari in any frame. The species page's word predates the
ruling, and the three story-bible lines that repeat it (`species-design.md`,
*For contrast*; `civilian-dress.md`, *Mnemari, for contrast*;
`five-o-second-season-treatment.md`, §2) each cite the page and nothing
else. So what the record states of the body, read under its own rulings, is
one negative and one compatibility: not the human frame, and able to live in
a standard oxygen habitat, which the Verdani also can. No world page exists
(Ilenne has none), no ecology, no sense the body is built around. A portrait
prompt written tonight would have to invent the form, which is the drift
`species-design.md` was started on 13 August to stop, and a form invented in
a prompt becomes the people's body by the first filed frame. The 16 October
rule's logic applies: the page is complete without a portrait, not pending,
until a page states the body.

**Settled by Fable under *Who approves whom*, his to overrule:** the ruling
governs the word; the Mnemari are not on the human frame, and the species
page's *humanoid* is owed a clarification (a word from before the ruling,
not a canon commitment) in a later PR, once a body exists to say it better
with. Recorded in `open-questions.md` with the options.

**What is fixed for the prompt whenever it is written**, so the body design
is the only thing owed:

  species card (`src/images/lore/mnemari.jpg`), and a card is never a

- **`ulessa.jpg`** — Mnemari, treaty-witness of Ilenne, requested to Federation assembly sessions that revisit old compacts; *what was said is hers, and what it meant is theirs.*

the negative. § 20's *what failed on the way* is kept whole: a limb laid on a
table returns a human hand, so the limbs hang curled; a headless body reads
as a frog and a short neck as a hippo, so the neck is long and the head is on
it; big eyes make it cute; a person creeps in at the edge unless the chairs
are said to be empty; grey and muted make the frame drab, so the colour is
natural and full and the room is neutral so that the hide carries it. **What
makes her a different individual**, under the identity rule and the one-face
rule, is the one thing the species page allows: the Mnemari show no marks of
age, healed injuries show as pale seams, and a witness past her eleventh
century has survived more accidents than one past her second. Ulessa's filed
frame carries two seams; Osune's carries several, named and placed, and
nothing else on her body says old. The hide's banding is given a little
darker and the russet a little deeper than Ulessa's, as one animal differs
from another, and that is the whole of the difference in the body.

**The place and the work, from her page and the entry.** Not an assembly
room, which is Ulessa's frame and the identity rule's first trap. A room on
Ilenne where she sits as a witness of last resort: a dispute has wanted a
memory nobody can contest, the parties have asked, and she has given the
words in the order they were said and stopped. The record gives no Mnemari
architecture, so the room is given in the record's idiom for a kept shared
space and in the materials the world page allows, dry pale stone of the
uplands, with nothing that announces itself: a plain room, a low plain bench
along one wall for bodies that sit, empty, no table before her since a
Mnemari stands and she needs nothing to read from, no sheets, no recorder,
no seal, no lettering. The parties are out of frame past the camera, the way
Ulessa's chair is, and the bench is empty, so that the generator is told
twice that nobody else is in the room.

page is owed a portrait under the 7 October rule, and a prompt where a

human reads is met by the body's posture alone.

**The body is the species page's and `species-design.md`'s, as the five filed

on 11 October, Kettsa on 19 October): small, forearm-to-torso length,
six-limbed, exoskeletal, low and dense, a low domed segmented carapace on six
jointed legs of equal kind, no torso, no shoulders, no upright posture, fine
sensory ridges along each leg and the lower carapace, a smooth rounded head

a modest range of tone within slate and bronze, never by pattern. Akkit's are
a cutter's and a scaffold engineer's, decades of both, and they sit where the

**Nothing worn.** Akkit is out of Corps service, and a Chthonari civilian

### 27. Missing lore illustrations — the powered load frame, an inline figure for the uniform page (written 23 October 2026, Opus; generated and filed the same day)

Dermot, 23 October 2026, verbatim: *"Write an image prompt for the powered load frame"*, the same day he ruled the frame canon as *job kit, not uniform* (`intake-2026-10-23.md`). The frame is defined in *What the Shell Does, and Where It Stops* on `src/lore/rank-insignia-and-uniform.md`. The page keeps its emblem card as its header, so this picture is an **inline figure in that section**, after the *It does not move her* paragraph, the way `stillwater-first-hall.jpg` sits in its page. The figure is landscape, 1600 px on the long edge, at finish strength 1.

**Why this prompt is Opus's.** Under *Which model does which work*, a prompt whose content is mostly physics and geometry is Opus's (Dermot's *"Option A"*, 16 October). The frame is an artefact: where the load goes, how the joints lock, and what it is not. The Ranger in it is anonymous and seen from behind, and her presence does not carry the picture. **Generator exemption** (3 September): no camera can photograph a 29th-century load frame, so a generator may make it.

**What the page fixes, and the prompt quotes:**
- worn over the shell, as a pressure suit is, and handed back after the job;
- no mind in it, and the wearer's own movement drives it;
- every joint locks safe without power and opens by hand;
- built to lift and brace, not to strike, so not armour;
- nothing on it lit.

**The shell under it** is the Engineering Corps': graphite with steel seam piping, with a plain rank tab seated proud of the chest and nothing else on it (`rank-insignia-and-uniform.md`, *The Uniform*; `uniforms-and-insignia.md`). **The job** is the page's own example: a rescue under a fallen bulkhead, here a buckled deck plate held up so a crawlway stays open. **The place** is pressurised, so the hood is down and the hair is tied back. The place is kept, not wrecked: one panel down in an otherwise sound compartment. That follows the *well kept* rule (11 October). The page names a fallen bulkhead, which justifies the one damaged thing, and the tone rule keeps anyone who was hurt out of frame.

**Readings taken for the frame** (Opus's, each his to overrule; none is written to the page):
- **The load path is visible.** Struts run from the arms down the back to a hip frame and down each leg to broad foot plates on the deck. That is where a lifted load has to go, and the generator's floating gauntlets fail because the picture shows the frame doing no work.
- **The joint locks are hardware you can see**: a lever or pin housing at each knee, hip and elbow, unlit.
- **The Ranger is three-quarters from behind**, face mostly turned away to the work. That meets the 28 July guardrails and keeps the frame as the subject.
- **Engineering graphite on the frame itself as well as the shell**, matte. Corps colour runs through the kit, as it does through a pressure suit.

- **`powered-load-frame.jpg`** — the Engineering and Safety Corps' powered load frame at a rescue; inline figure in *What the Shell Does, and Where It Stops*.
  > Documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light, 16:9 landscape, at work, never posed, nothing that invites the viewer. A Ranger of an interstellar rescue and survey service, seen three-quarters from behind and a little to one side at a working distance of three or four metres, wearing a powered load frame over her field uniform and holding up a heavy fallen deck plate so that a low crawlway beneath it stays open. The uniform: a modular matte shell in dark graphite with thin steel-grey seam piping over a close thermal liner, high collar with the hood stowed and down, sealed seams, practical and unornamented; one small hard-edged plain metal rank tab with two short horizontal bars, seated proud of the chest and seen at the edge of the frame; no other marks, no badges, no lettering. Her hair is tied back; her face is mostly turned away toward the plate. The load frame: an industrial exoskeletal frame of matte graphite composite and dull steel, worn over the shell, never in place of it. Plain straight struts run from the forearms up over the shoulders, down a spine beam to a rigid hip frame, then down the outside of each leg to broad flat foot plates set square on the deck. A squared mechanical lock housing with a plain manual lever sits at each elbow, hip and knee. Cushioned straps pass across the shoulders, waist and thighs, and a slim flat power pack sits low on the spine beam. Everything is functional, honestly made and well maintained, with small scuffs of use. The frame takes the weight: her arms are braced up under the edge of the plate, her knees are slightly bent and locked, and the struts carry the load straight down into the deck. ### 28. Missing portraits — Mhoren, the second Ovruhn the record names (written 23 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generated and filed the same day)

`src/characters/mhoren.md` landed in the same PR as this prompt, with the
fifth entry of *Histories in their own voices*, `src/codex/the-quiet-has-no-far-side.md`:
a keeper of the oldest chorus of Thavren, the chorus that carries the Ovruhn
history, who gave it at one recital with the Archive's translation desk
present. An Ovruhn has a body, and the people's page describes it, so the
page is owed a portrait under the 7 October rule, and a prompt where a
person's presence carries the frame is Fable's here (`CLAUDE.md`, *Which
model does which work*). Same form as § 17's `vhen.jpg` and §§ 19 to 26: a
documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera,
available light, **16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 through
`import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at finish strength 1; at work, never posed,
the 28 July guardrails met by the work, the modesty bar met by the body
(nothing is worn: `civilian-dress.md`, Ovruhn, a role is heard and not worn,
and Mhoren is not in Corps service). No image is generated by this entry;
the page carries no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**The body is the people's page's, point for point** (`lore/ovruhn.md`), as
Vhen's prompt gives it: among the largest bodies in Corps service, a broad,
deep-chested quadruped mass standing lower than its bulk suggests, the
forebody carrying a fan of boneless handling tendrils, stronger than a hoist
at the root and finer than a human hand at the tip; no face to address; the
hide of the flanks is the ear; a pair of small, mild eyes for the short range
the haze permits; a chest of layered resonant chambers. **The Vhen lesson
governs the frame** (§ 17, rounds 1 to 4): three whole-body rounds each drew
an elephant with the tendrils hanging from a face like a trunk, whatever the
negatives said, and the frame that filed showed part of the body only, so
close that its outline was never seen. This frame does the same and shows a
different part, under the identity rule: Vhen's filed frame is the flank as
a wall of hide with the tendril tips resting on a kerb of worked stone; this
one is **the chest**, the keeper's instrument, seen from low and close beside
it, the ridges of the layered resonant chambers running across the hide, and
the tendrils hanging slack and curled above the bedrock, touching nothing
(the people-body-design rule: a limb laid on a surface returns a human hand,
and a working limb that hangs curled does not). The place is Thavren's, from
the same page: bright days under a permanent haze, light scattered from
everywhere, shadowless and sourceless, nothing seen sharply past a stone's
throw. The chorus is nearer than in Vhen's frame, since this is a recital of
the oldest chorus and not the pause of one keeper: several soft unresolved
grey masses stand within the stone's throw, out of focus, none with an
outline, which is the one-face rule met by the world itself. The date is
none: the record fixes neither the contact nor the recital, so the frame
carries the record's present and no year. The record names no Earth animal
for the Ovruhn, and the first survey's three resemblances were the
observers' (*The Thing Outsiders Get Wrong*), so the likeness rule applies at
full strength: the elephant, the rhinoceros, the hippopotamus, the walrus,
the bull, the bear and the octopus are refused by name.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to a page): **the hide** a quiet, uneven matte
mineral tone, a cooler grey-brown than Vhen's warm one, varying as any hide
does, with no markings that signal (`civilian-dress.md`'s proposed default,
and the identity rule against Vhen's filed frame); **the chest ridges** as
low broad bands of thicker hide across the lower chest, a hand's width apart,
since the page gives layered chambers and no count; **the tendrils** as a
dozen or so, hanging from the forebody's lower edge at the left of the frame,
all slack, curled a little at the tips, none lifted, since the keeper is
singing and not handling; **the floor** patient bedrock worked smooth and
nothing built on it, as Vhen's frame gave the meeting-ground and the page
says law is chanted and nothing of a building; **the moment** the recital,
which a still cannot show, so the frame shows a body that is sounding and
not moving: the tendrils still, the chest filling the frame, the chorus
standing in the haze; **the camera** at the height of the tendril tips, a
little below the chest, as close as a desk's recorder would stand with the
chorus's consent, so the body rises out of the top of the frame.

**If two rounds fail** the Earth-animal test, nothing is filed and the page
stays bare, as Vhen's did for three rounds.

- **`mhoren.jpg`** — Ovruhn, keeper of the oldest chorus of Thavren; *there is a quiet above us, and it has no far side.*
  > Documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light, 16:9 landscape, a close frame at work, never posed to camera: part of a very large living body seen from low and close beside it, so close that it fills most of the frame and its outline is never seen. The upper two-thirds of the frame, from the right edge to past the middle, is the underside and near side of a great deep chest: a curved mass of dry, matte, cool grey-brown hide, finely creased and grained like living skin, rising out of the top of the frame and curving away out of the right edge, with several low broad bands of thicker hide running across its lower part a hand's width apart, like the ridges over chambers beneath; there is no head, no face, no eye, no leg, no foot and no tail anywhere in frame, and the body's lower edge is below the bottom of the frame. ### 29. Missing portraits — Orisseth, the second Prismeri the record names (written 23 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generation waits on the desktop)

`src/characters/orisseth.md` landed in the same PR as this prompt, with the
sixth entry of *Histories in their own voices*, `src/codex/two-points-in-one-life.md`:
a Full Wings reader of an astrogation guild of Prismere, formerly a First
Wings scout, who gave the Prismeri history at a Survey Corps confirmation
table, hanging, by form and never by year. A Prismeri has a body, and the
people's page describes it, so the page is owed a portrait under the 7 October
rule, and a prompt where a person's presence carries the frame is Fable's
here (`CLAUDE.md`, *Which model does which work*). Same form as § 26's
`isserith.jpg` and §§ 19 to 28: a documentary photograph taken inside the
world by a 29th-century camera, available light, **16:9 landscape** at
1200×675 through `import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at finish strength 1; at
work, never posed, the 28 July guardrails met by the work, the modesty bar met
by the body (a Prismeri wears nothing on record: `civilian-dress.md`,
Prismeri, nothing on the membrane and nothing over the facet band; the body
is plate, membrane and claw). No image is generated by this entry; the page
carries no `image:` until the desktop step runs. The entry's own title card
is already made (`make-codex-cover.ps1`, stamp AS READ) and on the entry.

**This is the first photograph asked of a Full Wings Prismeri**, and every
lesson of § 26 carries: every photographic round of the Prismeri failed on
12 and 14 October (a dragon from text at any distance, a creature render from
a bat), and the people's page carries Halle Ostrander's paintings by Dermot's
ruling. **The body reference is the approved lattice-gathering painting's own
Full Wings figure**, cropped for this prompt
(`reference-art/prismeri-full-wings-lattice-crop-2026-10-23.jpg`, cut from
`src/images/lore/prismeri-lattice-gathering-painting.jpg` the way the First
Wings crop was cut for § 26), passed for the body plan and nothing else, with
its medium negated by name and its shell cropped out. **The facet band is one
continuous seam** along the crown; **the hand is a Y**; **the tendrils are
few, long and fine**, hanging from the back of the skull ridge and never from
the mouth or the chin, since the painting's tendrils sit low enough to read
as a catfish's barbels and a photograph will make them whiskers if the prompt
lets it. **The Levril test stands for this frame as for every Prismeri
picture**: an outline that reads as a dragon, a wyvern or a gargoyle (a neck
carrying a head, a tail, bat-wing spars on a lizard's body, a crest) fails
however photographic it is, and the gold-and-blue plate invites it harder
than the First Wings body did.

**The body is the people's page's, by structure and never by resemblance**:
a light, long body on a level spine; the wings the forelimbs, a strong veined
membrane from the long outer digit back to the hind leg, with the three free
clawed fingers at the leading edge as the only hands; long-toed prehensile
hind feet; a short neck, the blunt head carried close against the shoulders;
two large dark forward eyes set low and the facet band above them; no tail;
Full Wings, so hardened plate in worn gold and dull blue over the body, a
heavier shoulder than the First Wings frame, and the long crystalline
sensory tendrils growing from the skull ridge behind the band
(`prismeri.md`, *A Body for Thin Ground and Thick Air*, *The Second
Emergence*; `species-design.md`, Prismeri; `civilian-dress.md`, Prismeri,
surface colour fixed by life stage, *no glow, no long neck, no tail*). The bat
is the convergence the record intends and is negated as a species, not as a
structure. **The place** is the upper lip of a lumenspire at the edge of a
settlement, after dark, which the planet page gives: a tall tapering tower of
frosted mineral, lit amber from within and brightest at the base, the forest
glowing below bright enough to read by, and overhead, through the haze, the
Lattice, faint pale straight lines, arcs and a great circle among the stars
(`planets/prismere.md`, *The Lattice*, the filed `prismere-twilight-lattice.jpg`
and `prismere-luminous-towers.jpg`). **The work** is a reader's: hanging at
the top of the stand after the curfew, the one of the people the settlement
does not go out without, reading the sky that the tendrils read without
looking at it. Nothing is held and nothing is lit by hand.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to the page): **the only being in frame**, no
second Prismeri, no shell, no First Wings, since the lattice reference carries
a pair and the 14 October rounds copied the shell in unasked; **the camera
from below and to one side at a working distance of several metres**, from a
lower ledge of the same spire, which is where the plates say a Prismeri at
rest is seen with the people's consent, the figure about two fifths of the
frame's height against the sky; **night**, with the forest's glow from below
as the key light on the plate and the underside of the wings, the tower's
amber faint beside it, and the Lattice the only thing in the upper frame,
faint, so that the frame is lit from below and threatened from above as the
people's page says the eyes are set for; **the wings part open**, as in § 26,
which is what stopped the hanging figure reading as a figure in a suit; **the
face in closed profile**, turned down toward the forest and away from the
camera, one half-lidded dark eye catching the glow, no mouth open and no
teeth; **the tendrils hanging**, five or six, long and fine as drawn glass,
falling straight down past the head from behind the facet band and catching
the forest light faintly along their length, touching nothing; **natural
full colour and normal exposure**, worn gold and dull blue plate strong
against the amber below and the near-black blue above, with *muted*, *grey*
and *drab* negated under the Ulessa lesson; **the moment** the reader still,
the sky moving too slowly to show it.

**Told apart from § 26** under the identity rule: night against day, Full
Wings plate and tendrils against grey-violet and none, a spire lip against a
working ledge, nothing in the hands against a lens and a glass, the Lattice
overhead against a hazy daylight sky. A variation that reproduces the First
Wings frame's composition, or the filed Full Wings painting's flight from
below, fails the identity rule before the body is read.

**If two rounds fail** the photograph test or the Levril test, nothing is
filed and the page stays bare; whether a Prismeri character page may carry
anything but a photograph is Dermot's and is not put to him here, as § 26
said.

who keeps a settlement's electromagnetic shielding sound, seal by seal and
loop by loop; at home in 2826 UCSD, in a settlement the record does not name,
never off-world, and the first person of the Imperium-remnant colony the
record names. A human has a body, so the page is owed a portrait under the
7 October rule, and a prompt where a person's presence carries the frame is

met by the work; under the 13 October rules the face is chosen deliberately

Prime, the colony*, added in the same PR, every line marked). No image is
generated by this entry; the page carries no `image:` until the desktop step
runs.

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** The page gives the colony's
irony in one sentence, *the colony shields itself carefully from the fields,
and shields the Spiralites from nothing*, and the picture shows the first half
only: a woman at the foot of a shielded building, reading a seam. No Spiralite
is in frame, no spiral habitat and no mine, since the record has not
established how anyone meets the people (`contact-design.md`) and a frame
that staged the harm would make a protocol case into a picture of victims,
which the worklist line and the cast principles both refuse. The Carillon is

rings visible to the eye at certain phases, and because it is the one thing

or scarred ground; cultivated ground in the distance in low rows, no crop
named.

**The place** is a settlement of the colony from the planet's page: buildings
built for electromagnetic shielding, which the prompt gives by shape, low and
long, faced in a continuous skin of dull matte panels whose every joint is
covered by a flush darker bonding band, with few openings and each opening a
deep sealed recess, and nothing standing proud of the skin, since a mast, a
dish or an aerial would be the opposite of what the building is for. The

recessed indicator and no screen; the stock forms (*handheld scanner*,

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to

### 31. Missing portraits — Idrun Hesk, the second Ilveth the record names (written 24 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generation waits on the desktop)

`src/characters/idrun-hesk.md` landed in the same PR as this prompt, with the
seventh entry of *Histories in their own voices*, `src/codex/shown-to-the-sky.md`:
a sealer of a buried working floor on Sardain, who gave the history of the
Ilveth in warmth, outside, at night, and glossed it in click-speech for a
Survey Corps reader. An Ilveth has a body, and the people's page describes
it, so the page is owed a portrait under the 7 October rule, and a prompt
where a person's presence carries the frame is Fable's here (`CLAUDE.md`,
*Which model does which work*). Same form as §§ 25 to 30: a documentary
photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light,
**16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 through `import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at
finish strength 1; at work, never posed, the 28 July guardrails met by the
work, the modesty bar met by the body (nothing is worn: `civilian-dress.md`,
Ilveth, what an Ilveth wears at home is not stated and would carry no light,
and Idrun Hesk is not in Corps service). No image is generated by this
entry; the page carries no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**The body is the people's page's, point for point** (`lore/ilveth.md`), as
`suvra-kel.jpg` and `ilveth.jpg` give it: long and low, several paired limbs
under a segmented body that keeps its mass near the ground, the forward
third rising into a hooded sensory crown of dry mirror-pits with a ring of
small photic eyes below it, broad vascular vanes folded along flank and
crown; the body runs at the temperature of the ground it stands on. The
settled figures carry over: five pairs of short limbs (`ilveth.jpg`), about
two people lying end to end and no higher than a standing person's knee
(the Suvra Kel brief, Dermot's *"size is fine"*, 23 August 2026). **The
Ilveth lesson governs the frame**: the people's picture went two rounds on
12 October and every variation read as a sculpted creature render lit from
the front, and Suvra Kel's own re-run on 11 October *grew a face the page
does not give*, so both filed images are held at Dermot's choice with the
gap recorded. The Vhen and Mhoren answer (§§ 17, 28) is the one thing that
has beaten a whole-body attractor in this file: **show part of the body only,
so close that its outline is never seen.** This frame does that, under the
identity rule against `suvra-kel.jpg`, which is the whole body at night on a
plain beside a frost-free outcrop. Here the part is **the crown and the
leading edge of one vane**, seen low and close, side-on, where the body
lies pressed along the foot of a low sealed wall; the rest of the body runs
out of the right of the frame unseen. The place is a sealer's, from the
people's page: shelter on Sardain is *not showing the sky your heat*, and
insulation is raised *to the level other civilisations reserve for art*, so
the wall is sealed to nothing, and the frost lies on every seam of it
exactly as it lies on the ice; there is no frost-free patch anywhere in
frame, which is the identity rule and the craft in one. **The moment is the
work**: the crown is turned to the wall, the pits reading a seam for warmth,
which is what a sealer does; attention is on the wall and nothing is turned
to the lens. The light is Sardain's day's end, a bright dusk from a small
dim sun low and out of frame to one side, long blue shadows, a dark
violet-grey sky in the top of frame, no stars (Suvra Kel's frame has them).
The warm-write cannot be photographed: it is thermal, invisible to any
camera the record allows, so **nothing glows, nothing is lit, and the vanes
are folded flat**; a glow on the vanes is a false picture of the register.
The record names no Earth animal for the Ilveth, so the likeness rule
applies at full strength: the centipede, millipede, caterpillar, slug,
snail, woodlouse, trilobite, horseshoe crab, armadillo, pangolin and
tardigrade are refused by name, and so is the monk's cowl the crown became
in round 2 of `ilveth.jpg`.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to a page): **the hide** dull, dry and finely
granular, grey-blue with frost caught in the creases between the segments

bank of fitted dark stone with its joints packed and frosted even, since the

thin, matte, veined vane lying folded flat along the flank where it meets

and sturdy, every one in contact with the ground, none raised (a limb laid
on a surface returns a human hand; a limb that stands on ice does not);
**the camera** low, at the crown's own height, a metre or two off and
side-on to the wall, as a reader's recorder would stand on the ice while a

#### Teodora Brask

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** Her page gives a method and
almost nothing else: a ledger arithmetic in which every entry carries a check
computed from every entry before it, first seen under her name in Free Outer
Belt Coalition navigation logs in the war's first decade after 2303 CE (2503
UCSD); born 2281 CE (2481 UCSD) in the outer system, no settlement, no family,
nothing after the war. So the frame is the arithmetic and not the war: a
woman alone at a bare bench in a small compartment cut into the rock of an
outer-system body in the early twenty-fourth century CE, working a check by
hand. **The lettering rule's third move**, substitute: a log is a writing
surface and would come back lettered, so the work is carried by a line of
small plain matte counters laid along the bench, each the same, one held
between finger and thumb above the line's end, the next check being placed;
a tally, which the rule names as safe, and nothing written anywhere. **What
it is not**: no fleet, no bridge, no Coalition device, no banner, no weapon,
no armour, no uniform, no wounded, no battle, no second person; the
Coalition's independence and the Inner System Defence Fleet are on her page
and nowhere in the picture, because the page says her method crossed the
line and the picture must not say how. **History.** The frame is exempt from
the hint rule and must still not be ours: no computer, screen, keyboard,
tablet, paper or office; and not the record's present either: no habitat
ring, no seamless coved composite, since a Belt compartment of 2311 CE is
cut rock lined where it must be.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to the page): the year 2311 CE (2511 UCSD), the
war's first decade and the method's, so she is thirty; a long bony face, a
prominent nose with a bump at the bridge, deep-set dark eyes, straight dark
brows, a wide thin mouth, pale skin with the matte pallor of a life without
daylight, dark hair drawn back tight into a short knot at the nape, a lean
build, chosen against Sunniva Holm's broad fair freckled face, Tare's long
still face with jaw-length hair and Winifred Adebayo's close-cut grey, so she
is nobody else's; heritage not on the page and not written; a close-fitting
work jacket of plain matte dark grey cloth with a stand collar and no visible
fastening, sleeves to the wrist, over plain dark trousers, the Belt line's
*nothing loose to catch*, nothing worn that carries a mark, a light or a
badge; the compartment small, its walls dark cut rock dressed smooth with the
broad shallow marks of cutting, a pale sealed lining panel along one wall, a
plain bench of dull grey metal, a fixed stool; one small round port in the
rock wall showing only the dark cut face of the body's next member a few
metres off, lit from the compartment, no stars; light from a concealed source
above the bench, cool and even, the corners dark; the counters small flat
discs of a dull dark grey, a dozen in a line, all alike; the moment one held
above the line's end, her head bent, her other hand flat beside the line.

#### Pell Annerley

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** Annerley designed procedures:
how a question is put, who answers first, what a seat can gain by its answer,
tested by whether any seat could do better by defeating another than by
saying plainly what it wanted. The record places them among the outer
stations across the Imperium period (2571–2640 UCSD), outside official
channels, and holds the papers and almost nothing of the person. A paper is
a writing surface and would come back lettered, so the frame shows a
procedure as the one thing a procedure is before it is written down: **a room
arranged for deciding**. A small plain room on an outer station, a round
table with the same plain chair at every place and no head, and one person
standing with a hand on the back of the last chair, having just set it; the
design is the ring of chairs, and the empty seats are the seats the papers
address. **What it is not**: no meeting, no delegates, no second person, no
Imperium officer, no braid, no flag, no monolith tower through a window, no

teaching frame with the taught party outside it), and a human hand or boot
on the rock at the frame's edge would file the student as human. So the
frame is the tutor and the rock, and the teaching is shown by what the rock
is: **a chamber cut for proofs**, its ribs left standing from the native
nickel-iron in different lengths and sections, since excavation is
composition and a member is *left, not built*; the chamber is lit, dimly,
because students who see come to it, which is the one concession in frame to
anyone who is not Chthonari. **The body** is the species page's and
`species-design.md`'s as the six filed frames carry it, with `tikket.jpg` and
`tsikk.jpg` passed as references for the body only; **nothing worn**, since
Pekkat is no Ranger and a Chthonari civilian wears nothing, which also tells
the frame from Kettsa's at a glance. **What it is not**: no numbers, no
chalk, no board, no written proof, no instrument, no second creature, no
Earth insect, no mouth, no threat; no vessel, no stars, no window. **The
century is the body and the cut chamber**, which can only be the record's.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to

little bluer than Kettsa's dark slate and Akkit's pale warm slate, with the
bronze cast confined to the fine sensory ridges along each leg, so it reads
as a line of bronze on each limb and nowhere else; the wear a lifetime's
standing on tuned metal and not a cutter's: the undersides of all six legs
and the lower rim of the carapace polished smooth and even, no scuffing on
the forelegs, no chip, the segment joints clean with only a little fine
grit; a body a little larger than the filed six, since the page fixes no age
and a tutor of long standing may be a large one; the posture the striking
one, body pressed low on a rib's upper face, five legs down and the near
foreleg raised a little with its tip just clear, the dome of the head level
and turned along the rib and not to the camera; the chamber a cut hall of
dark nickel-iron whose walls carry the broad shallow marks of cutting and no
seam of manufacture, with several standing ribs left in the native metal in
plainly different lengths and cross-sections running from floor to the
unseen ceiling, Pekkat on the nearest, the others falling away into the dark
behind; dim, even, warm amber light from an unseen source, the Belt's colour
in the filed `akkit.jpg`, the far ribs barely lit; no made object in frame
at all; the only figure.

#### Vaurel

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** A Cerebraun philosopher of
evidence who teaches the Hegemony's survey classifiers one question, *what
has this reading survived*, answers in three parts each carrying its own
grade, and grades claims without arguing for them; of the home cluster, the
world not named, no age given, active 2826 UCSD; the record holds the
teaching filings through the Hegemony data exchange, in translation. The
frame is the question being put: Vaurel alone at a low broad bare teaching
surface in a plain room of the survey service, with **one small sealed
sample on the surface**, a reading before its grade, two upper limbs laid
either side of it and a third raised and paused, which is the posture of a
question in a body with no face; the fourth upper limb along the body. **The
body** is the species page's and § 13's point for point, since the body is
the people's and not Sohrel's, with `sohrel.jpg` passed as a reference for
the body plan only as § 14 did for Tavesh; **nine centres, one person, one
figure**, as the page's own rendering note says. **Nothing worn and no mark
of office**, which is the civilian-dress default for the Cerebraun, and **no
display**, since the formal display-language is reserved and a generator
asked for it draws neon; the skin is one quiet tone at rest. **The room is
windowless**, on Mireille Achterberg's precedent (§ 17) for a page that
places a person nowhere: a window would assert a sky, an air and a world the
record withholds. **What it is not**: no students in frame (the one-face
rule), no human, no classroom, no board, no screen, no instrument bank, no
Earth cephalopod, no Hegemony emblem, no mark of rank. **The century is the
body and the room**, as in §§ 13 and 14.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to the page): the resting tone a dull warm
sand-grey, one tone, a third resting tone beside Sohrel's slate-violet and
Tavesh's grey-olive, since civilian-dress open item 3 (ruled A) makes the
tone individual and ties it to nothing; the body a little larger than
Sohrel's and more creased at the limb bends, an old person's skin, since
the page gives Vaurel a teacher's standing;
the posture raised on the four lower limbs rather than resting on them, the
body held clear of a low broad platform, which is how this frame is told
from Sohrel's seated desk and Tavesh's crouch at an instrument; the sample
a single small smooth matte dark-grey sealed capsule the size of a fist,
lying on the bare surface between the two laid limbs, the only made thing
in frame besides the surface, no light on it; the teaching surface low,
broad, bare and of matte pale composite, shaped to the body, no screen, no
recess; the room plain, kept and seamless with rounded coving, a wide low
doorway behind giving the scale, dark, and no window; soft even light from a
concealed slot overhead, a little warmer than the Halyx office's; the only
figure.

The body is soft and boneless, a little more than the bulk of a seated adult human, low and broad, with an upper side and an underside and no front, the same from any side: no head anywhere, no neck, no face, no mouth, no pair of large eyes, only a low rounded central body from which eight limbs emerge in two tiers of four. The reference image shows another Cerebraun, Sohrel: take from it only the species' body plan (the soft headless body, the limbs that are uniform tubes ending in blunt rounded tips with no fingers, the small eyes along the limbs, the dry matte skin), and nothing else, not its colour, size, pose, desk or room. The lower four limbs are short, broad and load-bearing, and here they are braced so that the body is held clear of the low broad platform it stands on rather than resting on it; the upper four are longer and freer, the working limbs, smooth along their whole length with no suckers, no hooks and no tapering to a fine point, their inner surfaces the same skin as the rest: two of them lie along the bare teaching surface, one either side of a single small smooth matte dark-grey sealed capsule the size of a fist that lies on the surface between them; a third upper limb is raised above the capsule and paused, bent, its blunt tip a hand's breadth over it, the posture of a question being put; the fourth rests along the body. #### Corvin Ashdale

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** An Imperium-period fold
theorist (2560–2627 UCSD) under contract to one of the Inner System's legacy
shipyard families, the holding the Halvern Combine descends from; worked on
in-system fold staging, treating the gradient at a staging site as the
variable that decides whether an aperture can be held; proved that a scaffold
of his generation's kind could not hold a fold between stars; the proof filed
as commercial confidence; no birthplace, no place of death. The proof is a
paper and the holding kept it shut, so **nothing is written in frame and
nothing is on the table**: the frame is the theorist and the yard. A man
standing at a tall window in a plain working room of the holding's orbital
yard, his back three-quarters to the camera, one hand on the sill, looking
out at **a hull frame in build**, which is the thing his proof is about: what
his generation could make. The yard is **derived, not styled** (Conventions,
7 October): a long dark lattice of plain structural members, unlit, with a
hull's bare frame held inside it, lit hard from one side by the Sun and
nothing else, no glazed nose, no lit flank, no stars in a sunlit frame
because optics are optics; the fold itself is not a thing a camera sees, and
no scaffold, aperture or glow is drawn. The room is on a spun section, so the
floor is level and the yard hangs outside the window at an angle, a little
tilted, which is honest. **What it is not**: no Imperium officer, no uniform,
no braid, no flag, no monolith tower, no weapon, no warship, no family crest
of the holding, no paper, no screen, no second person; no Eden passage and
no star route, since those came eighty-five years after his death.
**History**, exempt from the hint rule and still not ours and not the 29th

### 34. Missing portraits — Rhuven, the first Ovruhn Ranger the record names (written 24 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generation waits on the desktop)

people's page describes it, so the page is owed a portrait under the 7
October rule, and a prompt where a person's presence carries the frame is

**The body is the people's page's, point for point** (`lore/ovruhn.md`), as
the two filed Ovruhn frames give it: among the largest bodies in Corps
service, a broad, deep-chested quadruped mass standing lower than its bulk
suggests, the forebody carrying a fan of boneless handling tendrils, stronger
than a hoist at the root and finer than a human hand at the tip; no face to
address; the hide of the flanks is the ear; a pair of small, mild eyes for
the short range; a chest of layered resonant chambers. **The Vhen lesson
governs the frame** (§ 17, rounds 1 to 4, and § 28's two rounds): every
whole-body frame drew an elephant, with the tendrils hanging from a face like
a trunk, whatever the negatives said, and both filed frames show part of the
body only, so close that its outline is never seen; § 28 also found that any
floor under the body returns legs. This frame does the same and shows the

wall of hide with the tendril tips resting on a kerb; Mhoren's is the
underside of the chest with the tendrils hanging slack; this one is **the

and close beside, which is the one part of an Ovruhn the uniform page makes
different from the two keepers': the deep olive sections of the Survey
Corps' field shell along the top of the back and over the forebody, nothing
over the flanks, the four-bar pale grey-green tab at the shell's forward

mounted on the sections (`rank-insignia-and-uniform.md`; `civilian-dress.md`,

two of them lifted from under the shell's forward edge, wrapped once around

curled and touching nothing (the people-body-design rule: a limb laid on a
surface returns a human hand, and a working limb that hangs curled does

century is the shell**, and the shell is described by shape with its stock

### 35. Missing portraits — Hester Aldous, the first person of Winterbourne the record names (written 24 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generation waits on the desktop)

`src/characters/hester-aldous.md` landed in the same PR as this prompt,
filling the Winterbourne half of the Winterbourne and Saltmere line of the
14 October worklist in `open-questions.md` (*Human peoples and places with
pages and no people*): a Marlbrook-born shepherd who keeps the Marlbrook
parish flock on the high down of Winterbourne, where the turf is a product
of the sheep and goes to scrub within a decade if the flock is lost; at home
in the Albion system in 2826 UCSD, never off-world in any account the record
holds. A human has a body, so the page is owed a portrait under the
7 October rule, and a prompt where a person's presence carries the frame is
Fable's here (`CLAUDE.md`, *Which model does which work*). Same form as
§ 32 and §§ 19 to 31: a documentary photograph taken inside the world by a
29th-century camera, available light, **16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 through
`import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at finish strength 1; at work, never posed,
the 28 July guardrails and the modesty bar met by the work; under the
13 October rules the face is chosen deliberately against the cast already
filed and is nobody else's, every made object is described by shape with its
stock form negated, and the frame names its hint of the century. Dress
follows `civilian-dress.md`, *Dress by place* (*Winterbourne*, added in the
same PR on the Corryn Prime precedent, every line marked derived or
proposed) and the Tír na nÓg block's rule that *the crook is a tool, not a
costume*, applied here by leaving the crook out. No image is generated by
this entry; the page carries no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**What the frame is of, and what it is not.** The planet's page gives the
trade in one clause, *somewhere to run sheep*, and the frame shows the top
band of a parish strip with the one person who keeps it: a woman standing on
the open down near the crest of the scarp in late summer, side-on to the
camera and looking away along the slope at the flock grazing below her on
pale dry turf, and beyond the flock the ground falling steeply away to the
haze of the valley, where a line of small flint-and-chalk villages with
thatched roofs sits at the scarp foot, a couple of kilometres apart, each
where a spring comes out. The down is open turf and nothing else: no wood on
it, no scrub, no hedge and no wall, because the page says the turf is kept
open by the flock and chalk country builds no drystone wall; the one wood on
the record's high down is Winnow Hanger's, four kilometres from any spring,
and it is not in this frame. **The century is the sky.** High in the hazy
sky above the down climbs the thin pale trail of an ascent javelin, the one
quiet hint the lore frame `winterbourne.jpg` already carries at Dermot's
11 October ruling for the D2 places, and the only visible mark of its
century the page gives the world; the thatch's certification and the
current medicine show nothing. **The stock pastoral is negated by name**: the
generator reaches for a crook, a smock, a flat cap, a waxed jacket, a border
collie, a drystone wall, a hedgerow patchwork, a church tower and a tractor
on *shepherd* and *English downland*, and none of them is on the page; the
record names no dog, so there is none, and no church, so there is no spire
in the village line. No stream in frame, since from the crest the valley
floor is haze and a winterbourne photographed running would be a stream; the
dry gravel is the lore frame's and stays there. **No second person**, since
one would pull the eye and the page places nobody with her. The down is
**kept** under the 11 October rule and the 13 October settlements rule:
no litter, no wire, no track scars, no spoil.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his
to overrule, and none written to the page): late fifties, since the page
reads her birth as about 2769 UCSD from her working age; short and broad,
planted, a round weathered face with high colour in the cheeks, pale skin
lined at the eyes and mouth from a working life out of doors, light grey
eyes narrowed in the glare, white hair cropped short and bareheaded, chosen
against Tove Strand's freckled red-brown plait, Tare's long still face and
jaw-length black hair, Oriane Kessel's square weathered face and blunt-cut
dark hair, and Winifred Adebayo's readings (tall and spare, a long oval
face, dark brown skin, short grey-flecked black hair), so she is nobody
else's; a plain field jacket of dark blue-grey closely woven cloth with a
high soft collar, no lapels and no visible fastening, only a clean seam,
sleeves to the wrist, over a plain undyed shirt and plain dark trousers,
with boots whose leather is whitened to the ankle with chalk dust, the one
honest mark of the ground; nothing worn carries a light, a mark or a badge,
and nothing is carried in the hands, which hang at her sides or rest one on
the other; the camera a little below her and to one side on the slope, so
that she stands against the sky and the valley opens past her; the light
late-summer afternoon haze, warm and flat, a high thin sky with no hard
shadow; the moment a count, her head turned to the flock and her face seen
in three-quarter profile from behind, wholly on the sheep and not on the
camera.

**The body is the people's page's, point for point** (`lore/pelagene-littoral.md`),

shades a metabolism). No image is generated by this entry; the page carries
no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**This is the second photograph asked of a named Verdani**, and the first
one's history governs it. `isren-farrowkin.jpg` (above, *Missing portraits*,
the 7 October audit) took three rounds across 10 and 12 October: the first
read as a sculpture with glazed-ceramic vanes, the second grew a face on both
variations, and the third grew a turtle's mouth-line at one end of the body,
so the filed frame is a whole body small in frame, back-lit from across a
terrace room, a mound with no front end. The lesson of the 24 October
non-humanoid rounds is applied here instead, as the `nonhumanoid-portrait-prompt`
skill of 25 October records it: **part of the body, close, the outline never
seen**. The frame is of a vane, not of a Verdani. The camera stands on the
gate's works beside him and looks along the leading margin of one opened
vane toward the channel, so the vane fills the near third of the frame as a
broad, veined, olive-brown leaf with the mist-light coming through it, its
rows of small dark nodes along the edge in focus, and the body it rises from
is a low creased mound at the bottom edge of the frame, cut by the frame, with
no end of it in view, no rim, no front, no limb, nothing that could become a
face or a mouth. Beyond the vane, the one fact the frame turns on: the long
low pale line of the flood-gate running away across the channel into mist,
which is the planet page's own filed picture of the fenlands
(`planets/verdance.jpg`, century batch 11: *the long low pale line of a tidal
flood-gate, plain and seamless, the kind of works that keeps a stilted city's
water where it should be*), and, far off and faint through the mist, the
stilts and low roofs of a city standing out of the water.

**The body is the people's page's, by structure and never by resemblance**:
kinbeds carried on broad extensible vanes, held folded when the light is poor
and opened when there is sky worth taking; sensory structures distributed as
rows of small dark nodes along the leading margins where the vanes meet; a
low-slung, multiply supported body; no single face (`verdani.md`, *The Body
the Symbiosis Requires*; `species-design.md`, Verdani; the filed Isren
prompt's *low, broad, flat rounded mound* and *rows of small dark nodes,
evenly spaced, the only sensory structures it has*). **The colour is the
fenland strain's**: *the duller olive-brown of fenland strains adapted to
reduced light beneath marsh mist* (`verdani.md`, *Regional Variation*), so
the vane is olive-brown shading to dull bronze-green where the light comes
through, never the deep chlorophyll green of Isren's High-Reach lineage,
which is negated by name. Under the Ulessa lesson of 20 October the frame
asks for natural full colour and normal exposure and negates *grey*, *muted*
and *drab*, since a mist frame of an olive body is already at the drab edge

gate strong against it. **The vane is a living leaf, photographed**: fine
uneven veining, the light through it, a few dry brown margins and small
torn places, beads of mist on it, set into a creased grey-brown hide; clay,
render, ceramic, glazed pottery, plastic and silk are negated by name, since

grown as a token, by his 14 October choice. **The century is the gate**: a
made thing with no present-day stock form, described by shape, one long low

### 39. Missing portraits — Kesta Ul, the second Serephine the record names (written 25 October 2026, Fable, at Dermot's direction; generation waits on the desktop)

`src/codex/read-at-the-next-margin.md`: a Serephine Dunekin formerly of the
Star Rangers, at home on Kharis Belt IV, who wrote the history of her people
in the only hours her body is open, one part to each dawn and each dusk, and
sets the mirrors of a furnace at dawn and reads the melt at dusk. A Serephine
has a body, the people's page describes it and the record has photographed
one (`sethka-ru.jpg`), so the page is owed a portrait under the 7 October rule
and the form is a photograph, never moved off it by a failed round; a prompt
where a person's presence carries the frame is Fable's here (`CLAUDE.md`,
*Which model does which work*). Same form as §§ 25 to 38: a documentary
photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light,
**16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 through `import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at
finish strength 1; at work, never posed, the 28 July guardrails met by the
work. She is at home and off duty, so nothing is worn: the people's page
makes the closed body its own armour against the sky, and `civilian-dress.md`
(Serephine) has nothing worn outdoors at home. No image is generated by this
entry; the page carries no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**The body is the people's page's, as `sethka-ru.jpg` shows it**
(`lore/serephine-dunekin.md`; `images.md`, the `sethka-ru` entry): a low,
broad, sealed carapace about the size of a large dog, mineral-hard, no front,
held clear of the ground on six slender jointed limbs of unequal length
placed radially, not in pairs; many small dark eye-spots around the rim, each
glazed with a pale membrane; enormous thin translucent respiratory vanes that
unfurl from the upper surface only at a margin. **The identity rule against
`sethka-ru.jpg` governs the frame**, and the non-humanoid portrait rule of
24 October governs its composition: part of the body, close, the outline
never seen. Sethka's filed frame is the whole body on a high stony ridge at
dusk, halfway open, bone-grey, in cold light. This frame is told apart by
four things: **the hour**, dawn, the first low warm light from one side, the
night's cold still in the shadows; **the part**, the near rim of the carapace
and one limb filling the left of the frame and running out of it, with the
leading edge of a single vane just beginning to lift from the upper surface,
a hand's breadth open, the rest of the body out of frame; **the place**,
beside one broad plain polished panel of a furnace array, angled, its face
catching the first sun, its mounting out of frame, a line of further panels
soft and out of focus beyond; and **the surface**, a warmer pale grey than
Sethka's bone, with a dull sheen where long weathering has polished the
pitted hide, read as a difference between two people and the people's page's
*reflective* carried a little further, written to no page. **The moment is
the work**: the limb's tip rests against the lower edge of the panel, setting
it, and the panel's face throws one hard bright line of reflected dawn across
the carapace; nothing is turned to the lens, since there is nothing to turn.
The low sealed carapace on six limbs is the file's oldest Earth-animal
attractor and the frame refuses it by name: a tortoise, a turtle, a crab, a
horseshoe crab, a beetle, a woodlouse, an armadillo, a trilobite, a spider,
an insect, a sea urchin, a limpet. The mirror is the century's attractor and
is refused by name too: a heliostat farm, a solar panel, a satellite dish, a
mirror in a frame with bolts.

Readings taken for the frame (Fable's, under *Who approves whom*; each his to
overrule, and none written to a page): **the surface** a warm pale grey,
pitted and scratched, with fine grit in the seams and a dull pewter-like
sheen where the weathering has polished it, opaque, dry; **the limb** one
slender jointed limb of the same hide, its tip blunt, closed and plain, no
node, no claw, no pad, no fingers, resting against the panel's lower edge;
**the vane** the leading edge of one respiratory vane lifting a hand's
breadth from a seam in the upper surface, thin creased translucent membrane
with the low sun through it, the rest furled; **the eye-spots** a few of the
rim's small dark spots in frame, each glazed with a pale membrane drawn
part-way across, catching the dawn with a faint prismatic sheen, none
reading as a face; **the panel** one broad plain polished metal surface,
dulled by fine dust, angled to the low sun, filling the right of the frame,
its edge honest and unornamented, its mount out of frame; **the ground**
pale dry stony ground under a very clear thin sky going from deep blue
overhead to pale at the horizon, long hard-edged shadows; **the camera** low,
a hand's height off the ground, close, as a recorder set down beside the
array by someone in the record would see her.

**If two rounds fail** the Earth-animal or the photograph test, nothing is
filed and the page stays bare.

**The body is the people's page's** (`lore/veyr-basaltborn.md`): an open

iridescent sheen of cooled basalt, small compound eyes in clusters around

seam, taking load, and the fourth rests on the seam itself, still, as a
limb that is reading resonance rests, which is the people's page's own
sentence (*if a panel sounds wrong under strain, a Veyr trusts the
resonance*); nothing is turned to the lens, since there is nothing to turn.
The open lattice on slender limbs is the file's attractor and the frame
refuses it by name: a spider, a tarantula, a harvestman, a daddy-long-legs,
a stick insect, a mantis, a crab, a bundle of twigs, dry reeds, scaffolding,

refused too: pipes, valves, gauges, rivets, cables and a lit fitting.

### 42. Missing portraits — Elsha Rootkin, the first Verdani Ranger the record names (written 25 October 2026, Fable, by the daily Fable fill; generation waits on the desktop)

`src/characters/elsha-rootkin.md` landed in the same PR as this prompt,
filling the *A Verdani in or beside the Corps* line of the 14 October
worklist in `open-questions.md` (*Peoples the record says serve in the
Corps, or could, with no Ranger on record*): a Deputy Officer of the Survey
Corps' Ecology Branch, on the planetary survey crew of a vessel the record
does not name, on a watered world it does not name, in 2826 UCSD, who sets
the branch's instruments where she is told to and asks of every shaded plot,
before anything else, how much light reaches the floor. A Verdani has a body
and the people's page describes it, so the page is owed a portrait under the
7 October rule, and a prompt where a person's presence carries the frame is
Fable's here (`CLAUDE.md`, *Which model does which work*). Same form as
§§ 34 and 38, the two non-humanoid Ranger and Verdani entries before it: a
documentary photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera,
available light, **16:9 landscape** at 1200×675 through
`import-image.ps1 -MaxEdge 1200` at finish strength 1; at work, never posed,
the 28 July guardrails met by the work and the modesty bar met by the body
in the Corps' shell. No image is generated by this entry; the page carries
no `image:` until the desktop step runs.

**This is the third photograph asked of a named Verdani, and the first of
one in uniform.** The two before it govern its shape. `isren-farrowkin.jpg`
(the 7 October audit, above) took three rounds and is filed as a whole body
small in frame, back-lit from across a terrace room, a mound with no front
end, after round 1 drew glazed-ceramic vanes, round 2 grew a face and round
3 a turtle's mouth-line. § 38, Meril Duskkin, not yet generated, applies the
24 October non-humanoid lesson instead, **part of the body, close, the
outline never seen**, as a single olive-brown vane filling the near third of
the frame over the fenland gate. This frame keeps that rule and shows the
third part, under the identity rule: not a whole body in a room and not one
vane over water, but **the roots of the vanes where they meet the body, and
the Corps' shell and tab seated on the hide between them**, which is the one
part of a Verdani that the uniform page makes different from the two
civilians'. The camera is low and close beside the body, a little above the
hide, looking along it toward the open ground, so that the creased
grey-brown hide of the low body fills the bottom of the frame and is cut by
it, with no rim, no front, no underside and no limb in view; from the hide,
three or four broad vanes rise at the left and right and leave the frame at
the top, so no vane is seen whole and the body's size cannot be read; and on
the hide between two vane roots, small and sharp, sit the Survey Corps'
marks: two or three small fitted sections of matte deep olive shell lying
flat on the hide and following its creases, clear of every vane, one
carrying a small hard-edged plain pale grey-green plate with three short
bars, and another, apart from it, a small matte open-based triangle in one
plain finish (`rank-insignia-and-uniform.md`: a Deputy's three bars on the
survey track's insert; the Survey device, *a triangle, point up, open along
the base*, never where the tab sits). Beyond the hide, the one fact the frame
turns on: a plain closed grey instrument housing the size of a loaf, set on
bare pale ground at the edge of a stand of dark foliage that is not Earth's,
with no lens, no dial, no light and no lettering, where the page puts her
work, the branch's reading of the light at the floor on a shaded plot.

**The body is the people's page's, by structure and never by resemblance**:
kinbeds carried on broad extensible vanes, opened when there is sky worth
taking; sensory structures as rows of small dark nodes along the leading
margins where the vanes meet; a low-slung, multiply supported body; no
single face (`verdani.md`, *The Body the Symbiosis Requires*;
`species-design.md`, Verdani; the filed Isren prompt's *low, broad, flat
rounded mound* and *rows of small dark nodes, evenly spaced*). **The colour
is the canopy-belt strain's**, which is Isren's too: *the deep chlorophyll
green of high-canopy strains adapted to filtered forest light*
(`verdani.md`, *Regional Variation*), so the vanes are deep green with the
daylight through them, and the identity against `isren-farrowkin.jpg` is held
by everything but colour: the part shown (vane roots, hide and shell, not a
whole body), the place (open ground under a sky, not a terrace room with
glazing), the light (flat overcast daylight from above, not back-lit glazing)
and the shell, which Isren does not wear. Olive-brown is negated by name, so
that a variation does not drift to § 38's fenland strain. Under the Ulessa
lesson the frame asks for natural full colour and normal exposure and
negates *grey*, *muted* and *drab*, since a deep green body under an overcast
is at the drab edge by canon; the overcast is bright and even, the green
saturated, the hide warm. **The vanes are living leaf, photographed**: fine
uneven veining, the light through them, a few dry margins and small torn
places, set into creased grey-brown hide with pores and texture; clay,
render, ceramic, glazed pottery, plastic and silk are negated by name, since
the ceramic vane was Isren's first failure. **Worn things: the shell only**,
by shape with its stock forms negated: matte fitted panels lying on the hide,
a small hard-edged plain tab, a small open outline, nothing lit, no
lettering, no strap, no harness, no buckle, no pack, no saddle, no load; the
people's own answer is nothing worn and nothing grown (his 14 October choice

growth with no recognisable Earth leaf, no trunk, no bark, no flower, and
every Earth tree, fern and houseplant is negated by name. **The forest is the

### 43. Missing lore illustrations — Pelagos Minor, the basin after the Collapse, a header for the planet page (written 26 October 2026, Opus; generation waits on the desktop)

Dermot, 26 October 2026, verbatim: *"Write the image prompt for Pelagos Minor"*. The page is `src/lore/planets/pelagos-minor.md` (PR #1504, merged the same day). A place gets an illustration, so the page is owed one. This is its **header image**: landscape, 1600 px on the long edge, at finish strength 1, filed as `src/images/lore/pelagos-minor.jpg`.

**Why this prompt is Opus's.** Under *Which model does which work*, a prompt whose content is mostly physics, geometry or dates (a world, a station, a view from orbit) is Opus's (Dermot's *"Option A"*, 16 October). This frame is a world's geography after an event: a basin, an escarpment, a water level, three corridors, and nobody's presence carries it. **Generator exemption** (3 September): no camera can photograph a 29th-century launch basin on a world that is not Earth, so a generator may make it.

**What the record fixes, and the prompt keeps** (`s01e03c04.md` and the planet page):
- an **equatorial evacuation basin**, with ground above a **floodline** where the temporary shelters went up, on the **escarpment** where the Survey Corps station stands;
- **three launch corridors**, all lost in the Collapse, which ended when the **water came into the basin and settled**;
- on the sixth day the water lay in **a false calm over what had been somebody's neighbourhood** (Iona's block);
- the season is **Early Winter**, and the chapter opens at **dawn**.

**What the record does not fix, and the prompt does not assert:** the star, the sky's colour on an ordinary day, the vegetation, the building style and the population. Each is kept generic or out of frame. The three-coloured sky belongs to the storm. Six days on it is not shown, so the frame cannot say the fault persists.

**The corridors follow ascent-javelin canon** (`src/lore/ascent-javelins.md`): a javelin rides a **launch cradle** to near-vertical, and a spaceport *looks from a distance like a missile battery*. So each corridor is a long straight raised apron with short tilted cradle frames along it, low and empty. The 10 October ruling rules out a tower, gantry or tether, and the prompt negates each of them by name. Nothing is lit, because nothing in the basin has power.

**Tone.** The dark fact is that the water covers streets. The frame **hints at it and does not show it**: a faint regular grid of low pale rooftops and street lines under still water, read as order and not as wreckage. There are no bodies, no floating debris, no boats and no rescuers. The shelters are kept, orderly and clean, under the 11 October *well kept* rule. Nobody is in frame, which meets the tone rule, the people-and-place rule and the modesty bar together.

**Readings taken for the frame** (Opus's, each his to overrule; none is written to the page):
- **The viewpoint is the escarpment edge**, high and a little to one side, looking down and across the basin to its far rim. It is the shelters' ground and Rhuven's, and it is the ground a person stands on to watch the water settle.
- **The light is early winter dawn, low and pale**, from one side and under a clearing grey overcast. It is not golden hour, and nothing is dramatic.
- **The nearest corridor's apron is still just above the water**, and the other two show only as straight lines of cradle tops. **One of those lines has a gap** where its cradles no longer stand (the critic read of 26 October, applied as recommended the same day, Dermot having no fixed opinion): open water, nothing broken shown. The three losses can be read without anything shown broken.
- **The end of a row of pale temporary shelters** sits on the escarpment at the frame's near edge, cut by it, small and unlit. They say *afterwards* without a person.
- **The rock and ground are dark and bare**, with low sparse growth that is not an Earth plant. Every Earth tree is negated.

- **`pelagos-minor.jpg`** — Pelagos Minor's equatorial evacuation basin from the escarpment, on the sixth day after the Basin Collapse; header image for the planet page.
  > Documentary landscape photograph taken inside the world by a 29th-century camera, available light, 16:9 landscape, an inhabited planet that is not Earth, early winter, dawn. The camera stands on the edge of a high dark rock escarpment, a little to one side, looking down and across a vast flat-floored basin to its far rim many kilometres away. The basin floor is filled from rim to rim by one still, flat sheet of grey water, mirror-calm, settled, with no waves and no current, reflecting the pale sky. Just under its surface, faint and regular, the drowned order of a settlement shows through: a soft grid of straight street lines and low pale flat rooftops, seen only as lighter shapes beneath the water, quiet and orderly, nothing broken, nothing floating. Across the basin floor run three long straight launch corridors, broad raised aprons of pale composite laid parallel toward the far rim, each lined at intervals with short squat launch cradles: low open frames tilted up at a steep angle, empty, plain and unlit, short and stocky, never tall. The nearest corridor's apron lies just above the waterline as a long pale strip with its cradles standing clear. The other two are under water, showing only as straight lines of cradle tops breaking the surface. Along one of them the line of cradle tops stops for a stretch and resumes further on: a plain gap of open water where cradles no longer stand, nothing broken or floating, only absence. At the near edge of the frame, on the flat ground of the escarpment above the floodline, the end of an orderly row of small pale temporary shelters, plain rounded field shelters of matte fabric over light frames, clean and kept, cut by the frame edge, unlit, with no one outside them. The escarpment rock is dark, bare and weathered, with low sparse dark growth in its cracks that is not an Earth plant. The far rim of the basin is a long low dark line of escarpment softened by distance. The sky is a pale clearing grey winter overcast, thinning toward one horizon, where a low pale sun is just risen behind thin cloud, giving soft low light from the side. Stillness after an event; calm, sober, quiet, not dramatic. Natural true-to-life colour and normal exposure: grey water, pale composite, dark rock, pale shelters, a cool pale sky with a little warmth at the horizon. Photographed, not rendered: real atmospheric haze over a great distance, real water reflections with fine texture, real weathered rock, slight softness toward the corners, fine grain in the low light, a wide lens held level. Negative: people, figures, crowds, rescuers, soldiers, a person wading, a body, bodies, injury, blood; boats, rafts, rescue craft, helicopters, aircraft, rockets, a spacecraft, a vehicle, cars, a bus; floating debris, wreckage, rubble, collapsed buildings, smashed houses, rooftops with people on them, trees standing in floodwater, power lines, telegraph poles, a bridge, a road sign; Earth houses, pitched tiled roofs, a church spire, a skyscraper, a city skyline, futuristic towers, glowing domes, sci-fi spires, neon, holograms, lit windows, lights, glowing lines, a force field, a visible shield; a launch tower, a rocket gantry, a tall pylon, an orbital tower, a space elevator, a tether, a cable rising into the sky, a beam of light; a refugee camp with flags, red crosses, logos, aid-agency tents, tarpaulins, washing lines, litter; readable text, lettering, numerals, signage, labels, branding; storm, lightning, rain, a green sky, a copper sky, a split sky, a dramatic sky, a sunset blaze, golden-hour glamour, god rays, a rainbow, two suns, ringed planets, moons in the sky, a starfield; Earth trees, palms, pines, grass meadows, flowers, moss; monochrome, sepia, teal and orange grade, HDR. Render negatives: 3D render, CGI, octane render, video-game render, concept art, digital painting, matte painting, illustration, plastic sheen, over-smooth surfaces, glossy stock photograph. Landscape orientation.
  - **The test is the hint.** Streets and rooftops under the water must read as faint order seen through stillness. Wreckage, floating debris, a broken roof or anything that reads as a flood news photograph fails the tone rule on sight.
  - **No tower.** A tall cradle, a gantry, a pylon or anything rising toward the sky fails the 10 October ruling before anything else is read. The cradles are short and squat, and they tilt; they do not stand.
  - **Nobody in frame.** A figure, even a distant one, makes the frame a scene of the chapter and not a picture of the world. That would also make it Fable's, so it fails here.
  - **Not Earth.** An Earth house, an Earth tree, a power line or an Earth flood's furniture fails the place. A glowing future city fails the century the other way.
  - **The sky is after, not during.** A green, copper or split sky puts the storm back and asserts what the record does not.
  - **Triage:** first the hint (no wreckage, no debris, no bodies); then no tower or tether; then nobody in frame; then not Earth (houses, trees, poles); then the corridors (three, straight, short tilted cradles, the nearest above water, one drowned line with a clean gap and no wreckage in it); then the shelters (kept, unlit, no logos); then the sky; then the photograph test.
  - **Proposed alt** (to be corrected to the filed frame): *A vast flat basin seen at dawn from the top of a dark rock escarpment, filled rim to rim with still grey water, the faint grid of streets and low rooftops visible beneath its surface; three long straight launch aprons lined with short tilted cradle frames run across it toward the far rim, the nearest just above the waterline and the other two drowned to their cradle tops, while the end of a row of pale temporary shelters stands on the escarpment in the foreground under a clearing winter sky.*
